- duration: [Int!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)The trial timeframe. A value of 0 starts the subscription immediately without a trial period.
- durationUnit: [RecurringBillingSubscriptionTrialDurationUnit!](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--RecurringBillingSubscriptionTrialDurationUnit)The trial unit of time.

**RefundCreditCardInput**
Top-level input fields for creating a detached refund on a credit card.

- clientMutationId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An identifier used to reconcile requests and responses. 255 characters maximum.
- apiRequestKey: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An identifier to detect duplicate operations and prevent double-processing. This can be used to protect from submitting a duplicate request; for instance, after receiving an INTERNAL error where the ultimate state of the request is uncertain. If a request is made with a new `apiRequestKey` , it will be processed as normal. If subsequent requests are made with the same`apiRequestKey` , and the first request resulted in a refund being created (in any status), then the same refund in its current status will be returned.Subsequent requests with the same `apiRequestKey` must have the same input values as the original request. Subsequent requests with the same`apiRequestKey` must also be made after the initial request completes, and before 30 days has elapsed since the initial request finished. If a subsequent request is made while the first is in-flight or with different input values than the original request, it will result in a`VALIDATION` error on the subsequent request. If an`apiRequestKey` is reused after 30 days since its first use, it will be treated as if it has not been used before.If an initial request is made with an `apiRequestKey` , but the request receives a`AUTHENTICATION` ,`AUTHORIZATION` ,`NOT_FOUND` ,`RESOURCE_LIMIT` , or`NOT_IMPLEMENTED` error, and no refund is created, then no duplication will be considered. Subsequent requests with the same`apiRequestKey` will be treated as non-duplicate requests, just as if they were the first request with that value.
- paymentMethodId: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)ID of the credit card to be refunded.
- refund: [DetachedRefundInput!](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--DetachedRefundInput)Input fields containing details about the refund.
- options: [CreditCardDetachedRefundOptionsInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--CreditCardDetachedRefundOptionsInput)Input fields related to credit card detached refund processing.

**RefundInput**
Specific input fields for describing a refund.

- amount: [Amount](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Amount)The amount to refund. Must be less than or equal to the amount of the original transaction. Defaults to the total amount of the original transaction.
- orderId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The refund's order ID. Defaults to the order ID of the original transaction.
- merchantAccountId: [ID](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)ID of the merchant account that will be used when performing the refund.
- description: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Description of the refund that is displayed to customers in PayPal email receipts.
- lineItems: [\[TransactionLineItemInput!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--TransactionLineItemInput)Line items for this refund. Up to 249 line items may be specified. Only allowed for Custom Actions transactions.

**RefundSearchInput**
Input fields for searching for refunds.

- id: [SearchValueInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchValueInput)Find refunds with an ID or IDs.
- status: [SearchTransactionStatusInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchTransactionStatusInput)Find refunds with the given status.
- statusTransition: [SearchPaymentStatusTransitionInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchPaymentStatusTransitionInput)Find payments based on the time at which they transitioned to a given status.
- createdAt: [SearchTimestampInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchTimestampInput)Find refunds based on the time they were created.
- amount: [MonetaryAmountSearchInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--MonetaryAmountSearchInput)Find refunds with a given amount or currency.
- orderId: [SearchTextInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchTextInput)Find refunds with a given orderId.
- merchantAccountId: [SearchPaymentMerchantAccountIdInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchPaymentMerchantAccountIdInput)Find refunds processed through a merchant account ID or IDs. In most cases, this will be the merchant account of the original refunded transaction.
- customer: [SearchPaymentCustomerInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchPaymentCustomerInput)Find refunds with a given customer.
- disbursementDate: [SearchDateInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchDateInput)Find refunds by their disbursement date. Only use this search criteria if you have an eligible merchant account. Note that refunds can only be disbursed after they reach the SETTLED status.
- source: [SearchPaymentSourceInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchPaymentSourceInput)Find refunds created with a given source.
- settlementBatchId: [SearchTextInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchTextInput)Find refunds by the batch ID under which the refund was submitted for settlement.
- paymentMethod: [SearchPaymentPaymentMethodInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchPaymentPaymentMethodInput)Find refunds based on information about the payment method used for the refund.
- facilitatorOAuthApplicationClientId: [SearchValueInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchValueInput)Find refunds created by a third party via the Grant API using a given OAuth application client ID.
- userId: [SearchValueInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchValueInput)Find refunds with a user ID or IDs.
- storeId: [SearchValueInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchValueInput)Find refunds by the ID of the store that the transaction was processed in.
- readerId: [SearchValueInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchValueInput)Find refunds by the reader ID.
- shippingAddress: [SearchAddressInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchAddressInput)Find refunds by the shipping address.
- billingAddress: [SearchAddressInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchAddressInput)Find refunds by the billing address.
- disputeReceivedDate: [SearchDateInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchDateInput)Find refunds by dispute received date.
- processorAuthorizationId: [SearchTextInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchTextInput)Find refunds by the processor authorization code.
- processingMode: [SearchProcessingModeInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchProcessingModeInput)Find refunds by the processing mode.

This can be used to protect from submitting a duplicate request; for instance, after receiving an INTERNAL error where the ultimate state of the request is uncertain. If a request is made with a new `apiRequestKey` , it will be processed as normal. If subsequent requests are made with the same`apiRequestKey` , and the first request resulted in a refund being created (in any status), then the same refund in its current status will be returned.Subsequent requests with the same `apiRequestKey` must have the same input values as the original request. Subsequent requests with the same`apiRequestKey` must also be made after the initial request completes, and before 30 days has elapsed since the initial request finished. If a subsequent request is made while the first is in-flight or with different input values than the original request, it will result in a`VALIDATION` error on the subsequent request. If an`apiRequestKey` is reused after 30 days since its first use, it will be treated as if it has not been used before.If an initial request is made with an `apiRequestKey` , but the request receives a`AUTHENTICATION` ,`AUTHORIZATION` ,`NOT_FOUND` ,`RESOURCE_LIMIT` , or`NOT_IMPLEMENTED` error, and no refund is created, then no duplication will be considered. Subsequent requests with the same`apiRequestKey` will be treated as non-duplicate requests, just as if they were the first request with that value.
- refundId: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)The ID of the refund to reverse.

**ReverseTransactionInput**
Input fields for reversing a transaction.

- clientMutationId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An identifier used to reconcile requests and responses. 255 characters maximum.
- apiRequestKey: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An identifier to detect duplicate operations and prevent double-processing. This can be used to protect from submitting a duplicate request; for instance, after receiving an INTERNAL error where the ultimate state of the request is uncertain. If a request is made with a new `apiRequestKey` , it will be processed as normal. If subsequent requests are made with the same`apiRequestKey` , and the first request resulted in a transaction or refund being created (in any status), then the same transaction or refund in its current status will be returned.Subsequent requests with the same `apiRequestKey` must have the same input values as the original request. Subsequent requests with the same`apiRequestKey` must also be made after the initial request completes, and before 30 days has elapsed since the initial request finished. If a subsequent request is made while the first is in-flight or with different input values than the original request, it will result in a`VALIDATION` error on the subsequent request. If an`apiRequestKey` is reused after 30 days since its first use, it will be treated as if it has not been used before.If an initial request is made with an `apiRequestKey` , but the request receives a`AUTHENTICATION` ,`AUTHORIZATION` ,`NOT_FOUND` ,`RESOURCE_LIMIT` , or`NOT_IMPLEMENTED` error, and no transaction or refund is created, then no duplication will be considered. Subsequent requests with the same`apiRequestKey` will be treated as non-duplicate requests, just as if they were the first request with that value.
- transactionId: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)The ID of the transaction to reverse.

- deviceData: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Customer device information. Required when creating transactions using cards (only if using Advanced Fraud Tools), PayPal (only for one-time Vaulted PayPal transactions), and Venmo payment method types. This value will contain a Fraud Merchant ID as the unique, numeric identifier for a Kount account and a Device Session ID as the unique identifier for a customer device. - deliveryTimeframe: [ThreeDSecureAuthenticationDeliveryTimeframe](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--ThreeDSecureAuthenticationDeliveryTimeframe)Indicates the delivery timeframe if applicable.
- deliveryEmail: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)For electronic delivery, email address to which the product was delivered.
- shippingType: [ThreeDSecureAuthenticationShippingType](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--ThreeDSecureAuthenticationShippingType)Indicates shipping type chosen for the transaction.
- productCode: [ThreeDSecureAuthenticationMerchantProductCode](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--ThreeDSecureAuthenticationMerchantProductCode)Merchant product code.
- reorderIndicator: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether the cardholder is reordering merchandise purchased in a previous order.
- preorderIndicator: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether cardholder is placing an order with a future availability or release date.
- preorderDate: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)Expected date that a pre-ordered purchase will be available.
- giftCardAmount: [Amount](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Amount)The purchase amount total for prepaid gift cards.
- giftCardCurrencyCode: [CurrencyCodeAlpha](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--CurrencyCodeAlpha)ISO 4217 currency code for the gift card purchased.
- giftCardCount: [Int](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)Total count of individual prepaid gift cards purchased.
- accountCreatedDuringTransaction: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether the cardholder created the account during this transaction.
- accountCreateDate: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)Date the cardholder opened the account.
- accountChangedDuringTransaction: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether the cardholder changed the account during this transaction. This includes changes to the billing or shipping address, new payment accounts or new users added.
- accountChangeDate: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)Date the cardholder's account was last changed. This includes changes to the billing or shipping address, new payment accounts or new users added.
- accountPasswordChangedDuringTransaction: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether the cardholder changed or reset the password on the account during this transaction.
- accountPasswordChangeDate: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)Date the cardholder changed or reset the password on the account.
- firstUseOfShippingAddress: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether this transaction represents the first use of this shipping address.
- shippingAddressFirstUsageDate: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)Date when the shipping address used for this transaction was first used.
- transactionCountDay: [Int](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)Number of transactions (successful or incomplete) for this cardholder account within the last 24 hours.
- transactionCountYear: [Int](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)Number of transactions (successful or incomplete) for this cardholder account within the last year.
- addCardAttempts: [Int](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)Number of attempts that have been made to add a card to this account in the last 24 hours.
- accountPurchases: [Int](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)Number of purchases with this cardholder account during the previous six months.
- suspiciousActivityObserved: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether the merchant experienced suspicious activity (including previous fraud) on the account.
- accountNameMatchesShippingName: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates if the cardholder name on the account is identical to the shipping name used for the transaction.
- paymentMethodAddedDuringTransaction: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether the payment method was added to the cardholder account during this transaction.
- paymentMethodAddedToAccountDate: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)Date the payment method was added to the cardholder account.
- acsWindowSize: [ThreeDSecureAuthenticationAcsWindowSize](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--ThreeDSecureAuthenticationAcsWindowSize)An override field that a merchant can pass in to set the challenge window size to display to the end cardholder. The ACS will reply with content that is formatted appropriately to this window size to allow for the best user experience. The sizes are width x height in pixels of the window displayed in the cardholder browser window.
- sdkMaxTimeout: [Int](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)This field indicates the maximum amount of time for all 3DS 2.0 messages to be communicated between all components (in minutes). Minimum is 05. Defaults to 15.
- billingAddressMatchesShippingAddress: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether cardholder billing and shipping addresses match.
- accountId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Additional cardholder account information.
- ipAddress: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The IP address of the cardholder. Both IPv4 and IPv6 formats are supported.
- orderDescription: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Brief Description of items purchased.
- taxAmount: [Amount](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Amount)Tax amount.
- browserInformation: [ThreeDSecureLookupBrowserInformationInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--ThreeDSecureLookupBrowserInformationInput)Information about the cardholder's browser.
- installment: [Int](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)Indicates the maximum number of authorizations for installment payments. An integer value greater than 1 indicating the maximum number of permitted authorizations for installment payments.
- purchaseDate: [Timestamp](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Timestamp)Datetime of original purchase.
- recurringEnd: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)The date after which no further recurring authorizations should be performed.
- recurringFrequency: [Int](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)Integer value indicating the minimum number of days between recurring authorizations. A frequency of monthly is indicated by the value 28. Multiple of 28 days will be used to indicate months. Example: 6 months = 168.
- deviceChannel: [ThreeDSecureDeviceChannel](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--ThreeDSecureDeviceChannel)The channel for the transaction.

**ThreeDSecureMerchantInitiatedRequestInput**

**ThreeDSecurePassThroughInput**
Results of a merchant-performed 3D Secure authentication.

- eciFlag: [ECommerceIndicator!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ECommerceIndicator)The value of the electronic commerce indicator (ECI) flag, which indicates the outcome of the 3D Secure authentication.
- cavv: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Cardholder authentication verification value or CAVV. The main encrypted message issuers and card networks use to verify authentication has occurred. Mastercard uses an AVV (Authentication Verification Value) message and American Express uses an AEVV (American Express Verification Value) message, each of which should also be passed in the cavv parameter.
- xId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Transaction identifier resulting from 3D Secure authentication. Uniquely identifies the transaction and sometimes required in the authorization message. Must be base64-encoded. This field will no longer be used in 3D Secure 2 authentications.
- threeDSecureServerTransactionId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)3D Secure server transaction identifier resulting from 3D Secure authentication.
- version: [ThreeDSecureVersion](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ThreeDSecureVersion)The version of 3D Secure authentication used for the transaction. Required on Visa and Mastercard authentications.
- directoryServerResponse: [ThreeDSecureStatusCode](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ThreeDSecureStatusCode)The 3D Secure directory server response.
- cavvAlgorithm: [ThreeDSecureCavvAlgorithm](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ThreeDSecureCavvAlgorithm)The algorithm used to generate the CAVV value. This is only returned for Mastercard SecureCode transactions (3DS 1.0).
- directoryServerTransactionId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)A unique identifier for the 3D Secure 2 interaction with the card brand directory server. This field must be supplied for Mastercard Identity Check.
- network: [ThreeDSecurePassThroughNetwork](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--ThreeDSecurePassThroughNetwork)Specifies which network was used during 3D Secure authentication, so processing occurs on the same network. This is primarily for dual-network cards (e.g., eftpos cards). If not supplied, Braintree selects the network automatically, which, for dual-network cards, may not match the network used during 3D Secure authentication.

Input for transactions created with credit cards vaulted in an external vault, not the Braintree Vault. Do not use for transactions created from Braintree multi-use payment methods, or from single-use payment methods which will not be stored in an external vault.

- status: [ExternalVaultStatus!](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--ExternalVaultStatus)The credit card's assocation with an external vault.

If the`status` is`VAULTED` , but the customer is directly initiating the charge, do not pass this value.

**TransactionInput**
Input fields for creating a transaction.

- amount: [Amount!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Amount)Billing amount of the request. This value must be greater than 0, and must match the currency format of the merchant account. This can only contain numbers and one decimal point (e.g. x.xx). Can't be greater than the maximum allowed by the processor.
- merchantAccountId: [ID](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)Merchant account ID used to process the transaction. Currency is also determined by merchant account ID. If no merchant account ID is specified, we will use your default merchant account.
- orderId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Additional information about the transaction. On PayPal transactions, this field maps to the PayPal invoice number. PayPal invoice numbers must be unique in your PayPal business account. Maximum 255 characters or 127 for PayPal transactions.
- exchangeRateQuoteId: [ID](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)ID of exchange rate quote to be used for the transaction.
- purchaseOrderNumber: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)A purchase order identification value you associate with this transaction. *Required for Level 2 processing* .
- riskData: [RiskDataInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--RiskDataInput)Customer device information, which is sent directly to supported processors for fraud analysis.
- customFields: [\[CustomFieldInput!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--CustomFieldInput)Collection of custom field/value pairs. You must [set up each custom field in the Control Panel](https://articles.braintreepayments.com/control-panel/custom-fields#creating-a-custom-field) prior to passing it with a request.
- descriptor: [TransactionDescriptorInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--TransactionDescriptorInput)Fields used to define what will appear on a customer's bank statement for a specific purchase.
- paymentInitiator: [PaymentInitiator](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--PaymentInitiator)The initiator of the payment. Payment can either be merchant-initiated or customer-initiated. If the transaction is an ecommerce transaction initiated by the customer, no value is passed.
- channel: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)For partners and shopping carts only. If you are a shopping cart provider or other Braintree partner, pass a string identifier for your service. For PayPal transactions, this maps to paypal.bn_code.
- customerId: [ID](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)If charging a single-use payment method, optional ID of a customer to associate the transaction with. If vaulting the single-use payment method, this customer will be associated with the resulting multi-use payment method.
- shipping: [TransactionShippingInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--TransactionShippingInput)Shipping information. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- tax: [TransactionTaxInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--TransactionTaxInput)Tax information about the transaction. *Required for Level 2 processing* .
- discountAmount: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Discount amount that was included in the total transaction amount. Does not add to the total amount the payment method will be charged. This value can't be negative. Please note that this field is not used on PayPal transactions. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- surchargeAmount: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Surcharge amount that was included in the total transaction amount. Does not add to the total amount the payment method will be charged. This value can't be negative. *Required for Visa Rent Discount Program* .
- lineItems: [\[TransactionLineItemInput!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--TransactionLineItemInput)Line items for this transaction. Up to 249 line items may be specified. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- vaultPaymentMethodAfterTransacting: [VaultPaymentMethodAfterTransactingInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--VaultPaymentMethodAfterTransactingInput)When a single-use payment method is used to create this transaction, it can be automatically stored in the vault after transacting. If this field is left blank, the single-use payment method will not be vaulted.
- customerDetails: [TransactionCustomerDetailsInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--TransactionCustomerDetailsInput)Customer information to be stored on the transaction and used for fraud protection. Use this if you wish to pass customer information on a transaction without creating an independent stored customer record in the vault. This parameter can only be used if you do not pass `customerId` , and if you are not using a vaulted/multi-use payment method. In other words, this field is only valid when the transaction will not be associated with an existing customer.If `vaultPaymentMethodAfterTransacting` is also passed, these values will be used when creating a new customer for the newly-vaulted payment method.
- processingOverrides: [TransactionProcessingOverridesInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--TransactionProcessingOverridesInput)The values provided will take precedence over any similar fields, and will only be used for processing. These values will not update any similar fields and will not be returned in responses.
- industry: [TransactionIndustryInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--TransactionIndustryInput)Industry data information. Only one of the three sub-input fields can be provided.
- acceptPartialAuthorization: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Controls whether to allow partial authorizations (or "partial approvals") for this transaction. Defaults to false.
- paymentFacilitator: [PaymentFacilitatorInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--PaymentFacilitatorInput)Details of the Payment Facilitator (mandatory for PayFac Merchants).
- merchantCategoryCode: [MerchantCategoryCode](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--MerchantCategoryCode)Merchant Category Code (MCC) used to classify the type of business associated with this transaction. Defaults to merchant account's configured MCC unless explicitly overridden during transaction creation.

**TransactionLineItemInput**
Data for individual line items on a transaction.

- name: [String!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Item name. Maximum 35 characters, or 127 characters for PayPal transactions. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- kind: [TransactionLineItemType!](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--TransactionLineItemType)Indicates whether the line item is a sale or refund. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- quantity: [String!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Number of units of the item purchased. Can include up to 4 decimal places. This value can't be negative or zero. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- unitAmount: [String!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Per-unit price of the item. Maximum 4 decimal places, or 2 decimal places for PayPal transactions. This value can't be negative or zero. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- totalAmount: [String!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Total price amount for the line item: quantity multiplied by unitAmount. Can include up to 2 decimal places. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- unitTaxAmount: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Per-unit tax price of the item. Can include up to 2 decimal places. This value can't be negative or zero. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- taxAmount: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Tax amount for the line item. Can include up to 2 decimal places. This value can't be negative. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- discountAmount: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Amount of discount for the line item. Can include up to 2 decimal places. This value can't be negative. Please note that this field is not used on PayPal transactions. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- unitOfMeasure: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The unit of measure or the unit of measure code. Maximum 12 characters. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- productCode: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Product or UPC code for the item. Maximum 12 characters, or 127 characters for PayPal transactions. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- commodityCode: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Code used to classify items purchased and track the total amount spent across various categories of products and services. Different corporate purchasing organizations may use different standards, but the [United Nations Standard Products and Services Code (UNSPSC)](https://www.unspsc.org/) is frequently used. Maximum 12 characters.*Required for Level 3 processing* .
- description: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Item description. Maximum 127 characters. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- url: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)A URL to information about the product. *Required for Level 3 processing* .
- itemType: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The type of the line item, i.e., physical, digital etc.
- imageUrl: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)URL to an image that represents the product. Max 1024 characters.
- upc: [LineItemUpcInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--LineItemUpcInput)UPC of the line item.

**TransactionProcessingOverridesInput**
Processing overrides are additional data fields to be used only for processing. Provided values will take precedence over any similar fields(e.g. `processingOverrides.customerEmail` takes precedence over the vaulted customer's email address).

However, these values will not update any similar fields (e.g. providing `processingOverrides.customerEmail` will not update a vaulted customer's email address). These values are not returned in responses.

- customerEmail: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Customer's email address to be used by the processor.
- customerFirstName: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Customer's first name to be used by the processor.
- customerLastName: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Customer's last name to be used by the processor.
- customerTaxIdentifier: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Customer's tax identifier to be used by the processor. It is the social security number analogue for the corresponding country.

- statusTransition: [SearchTransactionStatusTransitionInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchTransactionStatusTransitionInput)Find transactions based on the given transaction status transition times.
- createdAt: [SearchTimestampInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchTimestampInput)Find transactions based on the time they were created.
- amount: [MonetaryAmountSearchInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--MonetaryAmountSearchInput)Find transactions for a given amount or currency.
- orderId: [SearchTextInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchTextInput)Find transactions with a given orderId.
- merchantAccountId: [SearchPaymentMerchantAccountIdInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchPaymentMerchantAccountIdInput)Find payments processed through a merchant account ID or IDs.
- customer: [SearchPaymentCustomerInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchPaymentCustomerInput)Find transactions with a given customer.
- paymentMethodSnapshotType: [SearchPaymentMethodSnapshotTypeInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchPaymentMethodSnapshotTypeInput)Find transactions created by charging payment methods of the given type.
- disbursementDate: [SearchDateInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchDateInput)Find transactions by their disbursement date. Only use this search criteria if you have an eligible merchant account. Note that transactions can only be disbursed after they reach the SETTLED status.
- source: [SearchTransactionSourceInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchTransactionSourceInput)Find transactions created with a given transaction source.
- settlementBatchId: [SearchTextInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchTextInput)Find transactions by the batch ID under which the transaction was submitted for settlement.
- paymentMethod: [SearchPaymentPaymentMethodInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchPaymentPaymentMethodInput)Find transactions based on information about the payment method used for the transaction.
- facilitatorOAuthApplicationClientId: [SearchValueInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchValueInput)Find transactions created by a third party via the Grant API using a given OAuth application client ID.
- userId: [SearchValueInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchValueInput)Find transactions with a user ID or IDs.
- storeId: [SearchValueInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchValueInput)Find transactions by the ID of the store that the transaction was processed in.
- readerId: [SearchValueInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchValueInput)Find transactions by the reader ID.
- shippingAddress: [SearchAddressInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchAddressInput)Find transactions by the shipping address.
- billingAddress: [SearchAddressInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchAddressInput)Find transactions by the billing address.
- disputeReceivedDate: [SearchDateInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchDateInput)Find transactions by dispute received date.
- processorAuthorizationId: [SearchTextInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchTextInput)Find transactions by the processor authorization code.
- partiallyAuthorized: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Find fully or partially authorized transactions.
- processingMode: [SearchProcessingModeInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchProcessingModeInput)Find transactions by the processing mode.
- achType: [SearchACHTypeInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--SearchACHTypeInput)Find transactions by the ACH type used.

**TransactionTaxInput**

- taxExempt: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Whether the transaction should be considered eligible for tax exemption. *Required for Level 2 processing* .

**UpdateRecurringBillingSubscriptionInput**
Top-level input fields for updating a subscription.

- clientMutationId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An identifier used to reconcile requests and responses. 255 characters maximum.
- subscriptionId: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)The ID of the subscription to update.
- planId: [ID](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)Updating a plan only changes the association; the price is not automatically changed. You can only update to a plan with the same billing cycle. You can't edit the plan on a Past Due, Expired, or Canceled subscription.
- merchantAccountId: [ID](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)The merchant account ID used to create the subscription's transactions. Currency is also determined by merchant account ID and it must match the Plan's currency.
- price: [Amount](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Amount)The new base price for the subscription. Must be a positive decimal value (e.g., 10 or 10.00). Overrides the previous price. Cannot be changed if the subscription is Past Due, Expired, or Canceled. Currency is determined by the merchant account.
- numberOfBillingCycles: [Int](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)The number of times the billing cycle will be executed. Set to 0 to indicate the subscription never expires (bills indefinitely). Valid range: 0-999.
- paymentMethodId: [ID](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)The payment method identifier to use for this subscription. Accepts single-use or multi-use payment methods. A single-use payment method will be vaulted automatically.
- payPalDescription: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The description displayed to customers in PayPal email receipts. 127 character maximum.
- modifications: [RecurringBillingSubscriptionModificationInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--RecurringBillingSubscriptionModificationInput)How to apply add-on and discount modifications.
- overrides: [UpdateRecurringBillingSubscriptionOptionsInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--UpdateRecurringBillingSubscriptionOptionsInput)Optional execution flags for subscription updates.
- descriptor: [RecurringBillingSubscriptionDescriptorInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--RecurringBillingSubscriptionDescriptorInput)Update the bank statement descriptor fields.

**UpdateRecurringBillingSubscriptionOptionsInput**
Input fields for subscription update options.

- prorateCharges: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)A flag that specifies whether the change in subscription price should be prorated. If omitted, defaults to the merchant account's prorate upgrades/downgrades setting.
- revertSubscriptionOnProrationFailure: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)By default, if the transaction for the prorated amount fails, the subscription is reverted. If you would like to continue with the update to the subscription and add the prorated amount to the balance even though the transaction failed, you should set this field to false.

**VaultPaymentMethodInput**

- clientMutationId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An identifier used to reconcile requests and responses. 255 characters maximum.
- paymentMethodId: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)ID of an existing single-use payment method to be vaulted.
- verification: [PaymentMethodVerificationOptionsInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--PaymentMethodVerificationOptionsInput)Input fields that specify options for verifying the payment method before vaulting. Only applicable if the payment method is of a type that supports verification. For supported types, verification is performed by default. If the verification fails, the payment method will not be vaulted. For additional, payment method-specific verification options, please see other verification mutations such as `verifyCreditCard` or`verifyUsBankAccount` .
- customerId: [ID](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)ID of the customer to associate the resulting multi-use payment method with.
- threeDSecurePassThrough: [ThreeDSecurePassThroughInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--ThreeDSecurePassThroughInput)Results of a merchant-performed 3D Secure authentication. You will only need to use these fields if you've performed your own integration with a 3D Secure MPI provider (e.g. Cardinal Centinel). Otherwise, Braintree's SDKs handle this for you in our standard 3D Secure integration.
- threeDSecureAuthenticationId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)ID of 3D Secure authentication performed using the Braintree SDK.
- riskData: [RiskDataInput](https://developer.paypal.com#Input--RiskDataInput)Customer device information, which is sent directly to supported processors for fraud analysis.
- makeDefault: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)This option makes the specified payment method the default for the customer.

**VaultUsBankAccountInput**

- clientMutationId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An identifier used to reconcile requests and responses. 255 characters maximum.
- paymentMethodId: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)ID of an existing single-use payment method to be vaulted.
- verificationMerchantAccountId: [ID](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)ID of the merchant account to use when verifying the payment method.
- customerId: [ID](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)ID of the customer to associate the resulting multi-use payment method with.
- verificationMethod: [UsBankAccountVerificationMethod!](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--UsBankAccountVerificationMethod)Type of US bank account verification to perform.
- verificationAddOns: [\[UsBankAccountVerificationAddOn!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--UsBankAccountVerificationAddOn)Type of US bank account verification add ons.
- makeDefault: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)This option makes the specified payment method the default for the customer.
- achMandate: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Language used to prove that you have the customer's explicit permission to debit their bank account.
- achMandateAcceptedAt: [Timestamp](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Timestamp)The date and time when the ACH mandate was accepted by the customer.

**VoidTransactionInput**
Input fields for voiding a transaction.

- clientMutationId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An identifier used to reconcile requests and responses. 255 characters maximum.
- apiRequestKey: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An identifier to detect duplicate operations and prevent double-processing. This can be used to protect from submitting a duplicate request; for instance, after receiving an INTERNAL error where the ultimate state of the request is uncertain. If a request is made with a new `apiRequestKey` , it will be processed as normal. If subsequent requests are made with the same`apiRequestKey` , and the first request resulted in a transaction being voided (in any status), then the same transaction in its current status will be returned.Subsequent requests with the same `apiRequestKey` must have the same input values as the original request. Subsequent requests with the same`apiRequestKey` must also be made after the initial request completes, and before 30 days has elapsed since the initial request finished. If a subsequent request is made while the first is in-flight or with different input values than the original request, it will result in a`VALIDATION` error on the subsequent request. If an`apiRequestKey` is reused after 30 days since its first use, it will be treated as if it has not been used before.If an initial request is made with an `apiRequestKey` , but the request receives a`AUTHENTICATION` ,`AUTHORIZATION` ,`NOT_FOUND` ,`RESOURCE_LIMIT` , or`NOT_IMPLEMENTED` error, and no transaction is voided, then no duplication will be considered. Subsequent requests with the same`apiRequestKey` will be treated as non-duplicate requests, just as if they were the first request with that value.
- transactionId: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)The ID of the transaction to void.

**CreditCardDetails**
Details about a credit card.

- brandCode: [CreditCardBrandCode](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--CreditCardBrandCode)A static code identifying the card brand.
- last4: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The last four digits of the card number.
- bin: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The first 6 digits of the credit card number, known as the Bank Identification Number. If this card originates from a third party such as a wallet provider, this BIN may not be present and the PaymentMethodOriginDetails will contain a BIN instead.
- binData: [BinRecord](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--BinRecord)Information about the card based on its BIN.
- expirationMonth: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The month of the expiration date, formatted MM.
- expirationYear: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The year of the expiration date, formatted YYYY.
- cardholderName: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The cardholder's name.
- uniqueNumberIdentifier: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An identifier that uniquely represents any credit card number, for cards stored in a merchant's vault. If the same credit card is added to a merchant's vault multiple times, each will have the same identifier. This identifier will only be returned if the field "origin" is null.
- origin: [PaymentMethodOrigin](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--PaymentMethodOrigin)Additional information if the credit card was provided from a third-party origin, such as Apple Pay, Google Pay, or another digital wallet.
- billingAddress: [Address](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--Address)The billing address associated with the credit card.
- threeDSecure: [ThreeDSecureDetails](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--ThreeDSecureDetails)3D Secure information for the payment method.
- imageUrl: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)A URL to an image logo representing the card brand.
- brand: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The display name of the card brand, e.g. "Visa" or "American Express".
- cardOnFileNetworkTokenized: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether the card on file is network tokenized.
- paymentAccountReference: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The payment account reference (PAR) value, a non-financial reference number for the card.

**CreditCardTransactionDetails**
Credit card specific details on a transaction or verification.

- creditCard: [CreditCardDetails](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--CreditCardDetails)The details of the credit card itself.
- networkTransactionId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The network transaction identifier provided by the payment network. If this transaction was created in order to verify a payment method before storing it in an external vault, then this value can be pased when creating subsequent transactions with the same payment method.
- accountType: [CardAccountType](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--CardAccountType)For combo cards, what account type was used for this specific transaction.
- acquirerReferenceNumber: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)Reference value assigned to a card transaction once it has been processed.
- processedWithCardOnFileNetworkToken: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether the transaction was processed with a card on file network token.
- accountBalance: [MonetaryAmount](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--MonetaryAmount)The remaining balance in the account after this transaction. This field is only returned for payment methods such as prepaid cards.

- defaultPaymentMethod: [PaymentMethod](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--PaymentMethod)Customer's default payment method.

- paymentMethods: [PaymentMethodConnection](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--PaymentMethodConnection)Payment methods belonging to this customer.
- transactions: [TransactionConnection](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--TransactionConnection)Transactions associated with this customer. This includes transactions created by charging a vaulted payment method that belongs or belonged to the customer, or by passing a customer ID when charging a single-use payment method.

**DisbursementDetails**
Disbursement details contain information about how and when the transaction was disbursed, including timing and currency information. This field is only available if you have an eligible merchant account.

- date: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)The date that the funds associated with this transaction were disbursed.
- amount: [MonetaryAmount](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--MonetaryAmount)Amount of money disbursed in the settlement currency, which may be different than the transaction's [presentment currency](https://articles.braintreepayments.com/get-started/currencies) .
- exchangeRate: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The exchange rate from the presentment currency to the settlement currency. If the currencies are the same, this will be 1.
- fundsHeld: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether funds have been withheld from a disbursement to the merchant's account.

**Dispute**
[A case raised by a customer to either request information about or to challenge a charge](https://articles.braintreepayments.com/risk-and-security/chargebacks-retrievals/overview). These are initiated via a customer's payment provider, such as their bank, and require a merchant to provide evidence or further information.

- id: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)Unique identifier.
- legacyId: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)Legacy unique identifier.
- amountDisputed: [MonetaryAmount](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--MonetaryAmount)The amount of money from the original charge that the customer is disputing. Can be 0. This amount is debited from a merchant's account and held in a third-party account until the dispute is resolved, at which time it is sent to either the merchant or customer.
- amountWon: [MonetaryAmount](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--MonetaryAmount)If an amount was disputed, the amount of money awarded back to the merchant if the dispute was reversed.
- caseNumber: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The case number for the dispute.
- createdAt: [Timestamp](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Timestamp)Date and time at which the dispute was created.
- receivedDate: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)Date the dispute was received by the merchant.
- referenceNumber: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The transaction reference number for the dispute.
- responseDeadline: [Timestamp](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Timestamp)The deadline for the merchant to submit a response to the dispute.
- replyByDate: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)The reply by date for the merchant to submit a response to the dispute.
- type: [DisputeType](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--DisputeType)The type of dispute.
- evidence: [\[DisputeEvidence!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Interface--DisputeEvidence)Evidence records submitted by the merchant for the dispute.
- originalDispute: [Dispute](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--Dispute)If this dispute is a follow-up to a previous chargeback or retrieval, the original dispute.
- processorResponse: [DisputeProcessorResponse](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--DisputeProcessorResponse)Additional information from the payment processor.
- status: [DisputeStatus](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--DisputeStatus)The status of the dispute.
- statusHistory: [\[DisputeStatusEvent!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--DisputeStatusEvent)A log of history events containing status changes by date for this dispute.
- transaction: [Transaction](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--Transaction)The disputed transaction which the customer is either requesting further information on or challenging.
- chargebackProtectionLevel: [ChargebackProtectionLevel](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--ChargebackProtectionLevel)The chargeback protection status of the dispute.
- protectionLevel: [DisputeProtectionLevel](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--DisputeProtectionLevel)The protection level of the dispute.
- evidenceSubmittable: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Indicates whether or not the merchant can upload evidence for this dispute based on its current status.
- preDisputeProgram: [PreDisputeProgram](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--PreDisputeProgram)The pre-dispute program of the dispute.
- remainingFileEvidenceStorage: [Int](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)The remaining storage available for file evidence on a dispute in bytes.

**DisputeConnection**

- edges: [\[DisputeConnectionEdge\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--DisputeConnectionEdge)A list of disputes.
- pageInfo: [PageInfo!](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--PageInfo)Information about the page of disputes contained in `edges` .

**EmvCardOriginDetails**
Additional information about an integrated circuit card (ICC) payment method supplied by an in-store payment reader.

- authorizationMode: [InStoreReaderAuthorizationMode](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--InStoreReaderAuthorizationMode)The authorization mode used to perform the transaction on the payment reader.
- pinVerified: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)An indicator for whether the transaction was verified via pin.
- inputMode: [PaymentReaderInputMode](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--PaymentReaderInputMode)The input mode used on the payment reader to facilitate an in-store transaction.
- terminalId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The ID of the terminal that was processed this transaction.
- applicationPreferredName: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The preferred name associated with the application used to process an EMV transaction.
- applicationIdentifier: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The identifier specifying which EMV application was used to process the transaction.
- terminalVerificationResult: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)A status code representing the result of a series of validations performed against an EMV enabled credit card.
- cardSequenceNumber: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)A unique identifier for credit cards that share the same PAN.
- applicationInterchangeProfile: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An indicator of the credit card's capabilities within the processing application.
- terminalTransactionDate: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The local date that the transaction requested authorization from the payment reader, formatted YYMMDD.
- terminalTransactionType: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An indicator of the type of transaction specified during authorization processing.
- cashbackAmount: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An additional amount associated with the transaction that represents the cashback amount requested by the cardholder.
- applicationUsageControl: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An indicator used to specify an issuer's restrictions for processing in a geographic region.
- terminalCountryCode: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The country code indicated by the payment reader to process the transaction with.
- applicationCryptogram: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The cryptogram provided by an integrated circuit card (ICC) used for processing the transaction.
- cryptogramInformationData: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An indicator for the type of application cryptogram provided by an integrated circuit card (ICC) to process the transaction.
- cardholderVerificationMethodResults: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An indicator of the cardholder verification method and if it was successful or unsuccessful.
- applicationTransactionCounter: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)A counter managed by an integrated circuit card (ICC) that provides a reference to each transaction using that card.
- unpredictableNumber: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)A value used to uniquely differentiate an application cryptogram used during authorization processing.
- issuerActionCodeDefault: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An indicator of the conditions that caused a transaction to be offline declined by the issuer, in a scenario where the transaction may have authorized if the payment reader made a processor request but was unable to.
- issuerActionCodeDenial: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An indicator of the conditions that caused a transaction to be offline declined by the issuer, in a scenario where the payment reader did not attempt to make a processor request.
- issuerActionCodeOnline: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)An indicator of the conditions that caused the payment reader to attempt to make a processor request.
- readerId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The ID of the payment reader that processed this transaction.
- storeId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The ID of the store where this transaction was processed.

**ExchangeRateQuote**
Details of the generated exchange rate quote.

- id: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)Unique identifier, which must be passed in the payment request in order to honor the exchange rate during settlement.
- baseAmount: [MonetaryAmount](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--MonetaryAmount)The amount in the `baseCurrency` to be converted to the`quoteCurrency` . If no amount was provided, then this amount is 1 unit of`baseCurrency` .
- quoteAmount: [MonetaryAmount](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--MonetaryAmount)The amount in the `quoteCurrency` converted from the`baseCurrency` .
If no amount was provided, then this amount is converted from 1 unit of`baseCurrency` , which will be the same as`exchangeRate` after rounding-off.
- exchangeRate: [ExchangeRate](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ExchangeRate)This much of `quoteCurrency` is required to buy 1 unit of`baseCurrency` . This includes merchant`markupPercentage` if any.
If a`markupPercentage` is specified, this field will be the sum of that percentage and the`tradeRate` .
- tradeRate: [ExchangeRate](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ExchangeRate)This is the rate at which PayPal will settle with the merchant.
- expiresAt: [Timestamp](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Timestamp)When the exchange rate quote represents expires.
- refreshesAt: [Timestamp](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Timestamp)When the exchange rate quote represents will be refreshed.

**GatewayRejectedEvent**
Accompanying information for a gateway rejected transaction.

- status: [PaymentStatus](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--PaymentStatus)The new status of the transaction.

- source: [PaymentSource](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--PaymentSource)The source for the transaction change to the new status.
- gatewayRejectionReason: [GatewayRejectionReason](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--GatewayRejectionReason)The reason the transaction was rejected, based on your gateway settings.
- processorResponse: [TransactionAuthorizationProcessorResponse](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--TransactionAuthorizationProcessorResponse)Fields describing the payment processor response. Depending on your gateway settings, the AVS and CVV responses may be the reason for the rejection.
- networkResponse: [PaymentNetworkResponse](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--PaymentNetworkResponse)Fields describing the network response to the authorization request.
- merchantAdviceCodeResponse: [MerchantAdviceCodeResponse](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--MerchantAdviceCodeResponse)Fields describing the merchant advice code response to the authorization request.
- riskDecision: [RiskDecision](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--RiskDecision)Risk decision for this transaction. If the gatewayRejectionReason is fraud, this may be the reason for the rejection.
- terminal: [Boolean](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Boolean)Whether or not this is the final state for the transaction.
- duplicateOf: [Transaction](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--Transaction)The original transaction if the gateway rejection reason was `DUPLICATE` .
- userName: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)User name of the person who performed an action that triggered the status change of the transaction.

**GeoCoordinates**
Coordinates describing a geographic position.

- latitude: [Float](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Float)The angular distance of a place north or south of the earth's equator. A positive value is north of the equator, a negative value is south of the equator.
- longitude: [Float](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Float)The angular distance of a place east or west of the meridian at Greenwich, England. A positive value is east of the prime meridian, a negative value is west of the prime meridian.

- billingAgreementWithPurchasePaymentMethod: [PaymentMethod](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--PaymentMethod)If the paymentMethodId passed to this mutation was a single-use PayPal payment method created with the [Billing Agreement with Purchase flow](https://developers.braintreepayments.com/guides/paypal/checkout-with-paypal/javascript/v3#checkout-using-paypal-billing-agreement-with-purchase-flow) , then this field will be populated with a multi-use PayPal payment method created alongside the transaction. Otherwise, this will be null.

- edges: [\[PaymentConnectionEdge\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--PaymentConnectionEdge)A list of transactions and refunds.
- pageInfo: [PageInfo!](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--PageInfo)Information about the page of transactions and refunds contained in `edges` .

- imageUrl: [URL](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--URL)URL to an image that represents the product. Max 1024 characters.

**RecurringBillingSubscription**
Represents a user's subscription record, containing billing status, pricing details, and lifecycle timing within a specific merchant account.

- id: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)The unique identifier for this subscription.
- legacyId: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)The legacy subscription identifier.
- payPalDescription: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The description of the transaction displayed to customers in PayPal email receipts.
- status: [RecurringBillingSubscriptionStatus!](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--RecurringBillingSubscriptionStatus)The current lifecycle state of the subscription.
- price: [Amount!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Amount)The base price and currency for this subscription.
- balance: [Amount!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Amount)The amount of outstanding charges associated with a subscription.
- billingDayOfMonth: [Int!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)The day of the month when the subscription will be charged on every billing cycle. Valid values are 1-28 or 31 (31 represents the last day of the month).
- currentBillingCycle: [Int!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)The subscription's current billing cycle. It is incremented each time the subscription passes the billingPeriodEndDate.
- numberOfBillingCycles: [Int](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)The number of billing cycles to execute. A value of 0 indicates it never expires.
- failureCount: [Int!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)The number of consecutive failed charge attempts by the recurring billing engine. Increments with each failed attempt and resets to 0 after a successful charge.
- daysPastDue: [Int](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Int)The number of days that the subscription is past due.
- timeline: [RecurringBillingSubscriptionTimeline!](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--RecurringBillingSubscriptionTimeline)Timeline information including billing dates and payment status.
- nextBillingPeriodAmount: [Amount](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Amount)The total subscription amount for the next billing period. This amount includes add-ons and discounts but does not include the current balance.
- trial: [RecurringBillingSubscriptionTrial](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--RecurringBillingSubscriptionTrial)Trial period settings for this subscription. Empty indicates there is no trial.
- descriptor: [RecurringBillingSubscriptionDescriptor](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--RecurringBillingSubscriptionDescriptor)The descriptive value on bank statements. This value may comprise static or dynamic information, and is passed on a per-transaction basis.
- planId: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)The plan identifier.
- paymentMethodId: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)The payment method to use for this subscription. Accepts single-use or vaulted payment methods.
- merchantAccountId: [ID](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)The merchant account ID used for the subscription.
- addOns: [\[RecurringBillingSubscriptionAddOn!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--RecurringBillingSubscriptionAddOn)The collection of add-ons associated with this subscription.
- discounts: [\[RecurringBillingSubscriptionDiscount!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--RecurringBillingSubscriptionDiscount)The collection of discounts associated with this subscription.
- transactionIds: [\[ID!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)IDs of transactions associated with the subscription, sorted by creation date with the most recent first. When returned in a subscription webhook, this array contains only the 20 most recent transaction IDs; otherwise, it contains all transaction IDs associated with the subscription.
- statusHistory: [\[RecurringBillingSubscriptionStatusEvent!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--RecurringBillingSubscriptionStatusEvent)Array of up to 50 subscription history events.

**RecurringBillingSubscriptionTimeline**
Timeline information for a subscription, including billing dates and payment status.

- firstBillingDate: [Date!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)The date when the subscription first started billing. For pending subscriptions with a future start date, this will be a future date.
- nextBillingDate: [Date!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)The date when the system will attempt to bill the subscription again. For pending subscriptions that have not yet started, this equals firstBillingDate. This date adjusts automatically with each billing attempt. For past due subscriptions with automatic retry enabled, this date will advance based on your configured retry settings.
- billingPeriodStartDate: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)The start date for the current billing period, regardless of subscription status. Automatic retries on past due subscriptions do not change the start and end dates of the current billing period.
- billingPeriodEndDate: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)The end date for the current billing period, regardless of subscription status. Automatic retries on past due subscriptions do not change the start and end dates of the current billing period.
- paidThroughDate: [Date](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Date)The date through which the subscription has been paid. It is the billingPeriodEndDate at the time of the last successful transaction. If the subscription is pending (has a future start date), this field is null.
- createdAt: [Timestamp](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Timestamp)The date and time when the subscription was created.
- updatedAt: [Timestamp](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Timestamp)The date and time when the subscription was last updated.

**Refund**
A refund of a charge on a payment method, representing an attempt to send money from a previous transaction back to the customer.

- id: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)Unique identifier.
- legacyId: [ID!](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)Legacy unique identifier.
- createdAt: [Timestamp](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Timestamp)Date and time when the refund was created.
- amount: [MonetaryAmount](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--MonetaryAmount)The amount that will be refunded, which can be less than or equal to the original charge amount.
- orderId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The order ID for this refund. For PayPal transactions, the PayPal Invoice ID.
- status: [PaymentStatus](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--PaymentStatus)The current status of this refund.
- processorResponse: [TransactionAuthorizationProcessorResponse](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--TransactionAuthorizationProcessorResponse)Fields describing the payment processor response.
- processorAuthorizationResponse: [TransactionAuthorizationProcessorResponse](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--TransactionAuthorizationProcessorResponse)Fields describing the payment authorization processor response.
- statusHistory: [\[PaymentStatusEvent!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Interface--PaymentStatusEvent)The records of all statuses this refund has passed through, with additional information on why each status occurred. Returned in reverse chronological order, with the most recent event first in the list.
- details: [RefundPaymentMethodDetails](https://developer.paypal.com#Union--RefundPaymentMethodDetails)Payment method specific details about the refund.
- merchantAccountId: [ID](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--ID)The ID of the merchant account that processed this refund.
- source: [PaymentSource](https://developer.paypal.com#Enum--PaymentSource)How the refund was created.
- refundedTransaction: [Transaction](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--Transaction)The original transaction that this refunds. If this is not present, then this refund represents a refund of a transaction that does not belong to this Braintree gateway account.
- paymentMethodSnapshot: [PaymentMethodSnapshot](https://developer.paypal.com#Union--PaymentMethodSnapshot)Snapshot of payment method details that will receive the refund, typically based on the original transaction. This will always be present. Equivalent to `refundedTransaction.paymentMethodSnapshot` .
- paymentMethod: [PaymentMethod](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--PaymentMethod)The multi-use payment method that will receive the refund. Only present if a multi-use payment method was used to create the original transaction and it has not been since deleted. The details of this PaymentMethod may have changed since the transaction was created; details used for the transaction can be found in the `paymentMethodSnapshot` field. Equivalent to`refundedTransaction.paymentMethod` (if present).
- customer: [Customer](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--Customer)The customer that the vaulted payment method (if it exists) belongs to. Equivalent to `refundedTransaction.customer` (if present).
- lineItems: [\[TransactionLineItem!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--TransactionLineItem)Line items for this refund.
- customFields: [\[CustomField!\]](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--CustomField)Collection of custom field/value pairs passed when creating the refund. Custom fields are [defined in the Control Panel](https://articles.braintreepayments.com/control-panel/custom-fields#store-and-pass-back-fields) . For all refunds except "detached refunds", these will always be null.
- descriptor: [TransactionDescriptor](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--TransactionDescriptor)Fields used to define what will appear on a customer's statement (for instance, credit card or bank statement) for this refund. This will always match the descriptor from the refunded transaction (if present).
- disbursementDetails: [DisbursementDetails](https://developer.paypal.com#Object--DisbursementDetails)The disbursement details associated with this refund. This field is only available after the refund is SETTLED and if you have an eligible merchant account.
- paymentInitiatedAt: [Timestamp](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--Timestamp)The refund date and time as reported by the in-store payment terminal.
- merchantId: [String](https://developer.paypal.com#Scalar--String)The ID of the merchant that processed this refund.

A reversal will attempt to void the original transaction if it has not yet settled. If the original transaction has settled, a reversal will create a refund for the full amount.

A single-use, tokenized value representing a CVV (card verification value), otherwise known as CSC or CVC. This cannot be charged or authorized, since it is not a payment method, but it can be used alongside a multi-use credit card payment method.
