Specifies which payment network was used during 3D Secure authentication to ensure the transaction is routed to the same network for processing. Primarily used for dual-network cards (e.g., eftpos cards).

Accepted values (case-insensitive):

- `eftpos`
- `Visa`
- `Mastercard`

The version of 3D Secure authentication used for the transaction. Required
on Visa and Mastercard authentications. Must be composed of digits separated
by periods (e.g. `1.0.2`).

Transaction identifier resulting from 3D Secure authentication. Uniquely identifies the transaction and sometimes required in the authorization message. Must be base64-encoded. This field will no longer be used in 3D Secure 2 authentications.

Specifies the source of the transaction. The value passed depends on whether the transaction is initiated by the merchant or the customer. If the transaction is an ecommerce transaction initiated by the customer, no value is passed.

Accepted values for merchant-initiated transactions:

- `recurring` = Transactions for subsequent recurring payments (e.g. subscriptions with a fixed amount on a predefined schedule).
- `unscheduled` = Transactions for unscheduled payments that are not recurring on a predefined schedule or amount (e.g. balance top-up). Formerly`merchant` .
- `installment` = Transactions for subsequent installment payments. (e.g. when the customer makes a single large purchase and wants to make payments over time).

Accepted values for customer-initiated transactions:

- `recurring_first` = Transactions that represent the first in a series of recurring payments or subscription.
- `moto` = Transactions that are initiated by the customer via the merchant by mail or telephone.
- `installment_first` = Transactions that represent the first in a series of installment payments.
- `estimated` = Transactions that support subsequent incremental authorization.
- 'estimated_moto' = Transactions that are initiated by the customer via the merchant by mail or telephone that support subsequent incremental authorization.

Note: `installment` and `installment_first` may only be available in certain regions.  If installment transactions are not supported in your region, the transaction will automatically be categorized as `recurring`.

[ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)format.

## Examples

### Full example

    Here is an example of passing in everything a typical merchant might use. Some parameters are
    mutually exclusive, so we'll show those in separate examples. If there is anything you want to store
    with the transaction details that we don't have a field for, you can always use

[Collect device data](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/premium-fraud-management-tools/client-side)from the client and include the deviceDataFromTheClient in the transaction.

1. Java

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest()
  .amount(new BigDecimal("10.00"))
  .orderId("order id")
  .merchantAccountId("a_merchant_account_id")
  .paymentMethodNonce(nonceFromTheClient)
  .deviceData(deviceDataFromTheClient)
  .customer()
    .firstName("Drew")
    .lastName("Smith")
    .company("Braintree")
    .phone("312-555-1234")
    .fax("312-555-1235")
    .website("http://www.example.com")
    .email("drew@example.com")
    .done()
  .billingAddress()
    .firstName("Paul")
    .lastName("Smith")
    .company("Braintree")
    .streetAddress("1 E Main St")
    .extendedAddress("Suite 403")
    .locality("Chicago")
    .region("IL")
    .postalCode("60622")
    .countryCodeAlpha2("US")
    .done()
  .shippingAddress()
    .firstName("Jen")
    .lastName("Smith")
    .company("Braintree")
    .streetAddress("1 E 1st St")
    .extendedAddress("Suite 403")
    .locality("Bartlett")
    .region("IL")
    .postalCode("60103")
    .countryCodeAlpha2("US")
    .done()
  .options()
    .submitForSettlement(true)
    .done();
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.transaction().sale(request);
```
1. Java

```
result.isSuccess();
// true
Transaction transaction = result.getTarget();
transaction.getType();
// Transaction.Type.CREDIT
transaction.getStatus();
// Transaction.Status.SUBMITTED_FOR_SETTLEMENT
```
### Storing in Vault

    When creating a transaction, you can also store the payment method in your Vault.
    #### Existing customer with new payment method

    To associate this transaction's payment method with an existing customer, pass a
    [customerId](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#customer_id)along with

[options.storeInVault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#options-store_in_vault)or

[options.storeInVaultOnSuccess](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#options-store_in_vault_on_success)as true.

1. Java

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest()
  .amount(new BigDecimal("10.00"))
  .paymentMethodNonce(nonceFromTheClient)
  .customerId("the_customer_id")
  .options()
    .storeInVaultOnSuccess(true)
    .done();
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.transaction().sale(request);
```
#### New customer with new payment method

    To store a payment method for a new customer, set
    [options.storeInVault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#options-store_in_vault)or

[options.storeInVaultOnSuccess](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#options-store_in_vault_on_success)to true on your transaction. You can optionally specify

[customer](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#customer)parameters for your new customer, as well:

1. Java

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest()
  .amount(new BigDecimal("10.00"))
  .paymentMethodNonce(nonceFromTheClient)
  .customer()
    .id("a_customer_id")
    .done()
  .options()
    .storeInVaultOnSuccess(true)
    .done();
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.transaction().sale(request);
```
[customer](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#customer)parameter should only be used when creating a new customer with a new payment method, and storeInVaultOnSuccess only vaults the payment method if the transaction is successful.

### Using a vaulted payment method

    You can create a transaction using a payment method stored in the
    [Vault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/vault/overview)by passing a

1. Java

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest()
  .paymentMethodToken("the_token")
  .amount(new BigDecimal("10.00"));
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.transaction().sale(request);
```
[customerId](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#customer_id), which will use the customer's default payment method:

1. Java

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest()
  .customerId("the_customer_id")
  .amount(new BigDecimal("10.00"));
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.transaction().sale(request);
```
### Using a CVV-only nonce

    To transact with a CVV-only nonce, use both a nonce representing the CVV **and**a

[paymentMethodToken](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#payment_method_token)representing the vaulted payment method. To collect a CVV-only nonce, use the client SDKs to tokenize only the CVV property. See an example in our

1. Java

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest()
  .paymentMethodToken("the_token")
  .paymentMethodNonce(cvvOnlyNonceFromClient)
  .amount(new BigDecimal("10.00"));
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.transaction().sale(request);
```
### Specify merchant account ID

    To specify which merchant account to use, pass the
    [merchantAccountId](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#merchant_account_id)when creating the transaction.

1. Java

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest()
  .amount(new BigDecimal("100.00"))
  .merchantAccountId("your_merchant_account")
  .paymentMethodNonce(nonceFromTheClient);
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.transaction().sale(request);
```
[Contact us](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/help?issue=TransactionProcessingQuestion)if you would like to change which merchant account is default.

### Using stored addresses

    You can use
    [addresses stored on a customer](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/address/create)by passing the address's ID. This works for both the shipping address and billing address.

1. Java

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest()
  .customerId("the_customer_id")
  .amount(new BigDecimal("10.00"))
  .billingAddressId("AA")
  .shippingAddressId("AB");
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.transaction().sale(request);
```
### Custom fields

    Whatever you
    [configure as the API name for your custom fields](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/custom-fields#creating-a-custom-field)will be used when setting them on the transaction. Here is an example of setting custom fields with API names of

`custom_field_one` and `custom_field_two`.
    1. Java

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest()
  .amount(new BigDecimal("100.00"))
  .paymentMethodNonce("nonce-from-the-cleint")
  .customField("custom_field_one", "value one")
  .customField("custom_field_two", "value two");
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.transaction().sale(request);
Transaction transaction = result.getTarget();
transaction.getCustomFields();
// {custom_field_one=value one, custom_field_two=value two}
```
### Dynamic descriptors

    Dynamic descriptors are typically composed of a name and phone number or URL. The name must include
    the business name, followed by a product name or identifier, separated by an asterisk (*). Depending
    on the type of transaction you're creating, the length/character limits may differ from those
    outlined above. For example, you can only specify up to 18 characters for dynamic descriptor names
    on Braintree Marketplace transactions. See below for details on [Venmo](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#venmo),

[PayPal](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#paypal), and

[Braintree Marketplace](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#braintree-marketplace)dynamic descriptors. Your processor may also restrict which descriptor values you can pass; certain processors allow you to pass URLs instead of phone numbers, while others accept only phone numbers or only names. If your processor supports URLs and you send both a phone number and URL, we will only pass the URL to the processor.

[Contact us](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/help?issue=updateDescriptor)for more information on your processor's specific requirements.

1. Java

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest()
  .amount(new BigDecimal("100.00"))
  .paymentMethodNonce(nonceFromTheClient)
  .descriptor()
    .name("company*my product")
    .phone("3125551212")
    .url("company.com")
    .done();
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.transaction().sale(request);
Transaction transaction = result.getTarget();
transaction.getDescriptor().getName();
// "company*my product"
transaction.getDescriptor().getPhone();
// "3125551212"
```
#### Venmo

    Venmo only supports the dynamic descriptor `name`. Its format allows alpha-numeric
    characters and `+-.`  (space included); any other characters will result in the dynamic
    descriptor name not being included in the full descriptor sent to the processor. The full descriptor
    submitted to the processor is structured as follows:
    - The default prefix of VENMO * (Two whitespaces).
- 
            The `Business Name` submitted in the[Venmo application form](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/venmo#go-live) .
- 
            The `Dynamic Descriptor Name` submitted in the[transaction.sale()](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/java/#descriptor-name) or[transaction.submit_for_settlement()](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/submit-for-settlement/java#descriptor) call.

`AStore` is the `Business Name` and `O-1234` is the
    `Dynamic Descriptor Name`. If the dynamic descriptor name contains invalid characters,
    e.g. 0#1234, the entire dynamic descriptor name will be ignored.
    `Business Name` and `Dynamic Descriptor Name` portion will be truncated as
        needed. If you want to change the `Business Name` of the descriptor, you can edit your
        Venmo profile via the Venmo Processing page in the Control Panel. This will also update the name
        displayed to customers in the Venmo app during transaction processing.
    #### PayPal

    For PayPal transactions only, the dynamic descriptor is limited to a total of 22 characters and includes the following
    elements:
- The default prefix of `PAYPAL *`
- Your PayPal hard descriptor*
- The product portion of your `name`

These rules apply only when the payment method is PayPal. Card and other payment methods follow their own descriptor rules.

**Depending on your PayPal account setup, the PayPal hard descriptor may not be included in the dynamic descriptor. You can update the hard descriptor value from your*

[PayPal console](https://www.paypal.com/login). The name must meet the following guidelines:

- Must include your registered Doing Business As (DBA) name, followed by an asterisk and a product description
- The DBA portion must be 3, 7 or 12 characters long - this portion will be dropped from your dynamic descriptor

#### Braintree Marketplace

    The only dynamic descriptor value we will pass for Braintree Marketplace transactions is the
    name you specify. We will not send any dynamic
    phone or url values to the processor, but we
    will pass the phone from the hard descriptor on your master merchant
    account. The dynamic descriptor name can only contain the ASCII characters a-z, A-Z, the numbers
    0-9, and the characters `.-+` and spaces (it can't contain special characters like
    `Ñ`, `ü`, and `é`). The maximum length is 18 characters; we will
    truncate any longer strings. The descriptor we pass to the processor will start with
    `"BT *"`, followed by the name you specify.
- 
            If the specified name is 12 characters or fewer, the descriptor we pass to the processor will
            end with a randomly generated 6-character string (e.g. `123abc` ) which identifies the
            sub-merchant:`BT *MYDESCRIPTOR123abc`
- 
            If the specified name is 13 characters or greater, the descriptor we pass to the processor will
            not end with a randomly generated 6-character string:
            `BT *MYDESCRIPTORISLONG`

### Hold a Braintree Marketplace transaction in escrow on creation

    Upon creating a
    [Braintree Marketplace transaction](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/braintree-marketplace/create), you can specify that its funds should be held in escrow. These funds can then be

[released](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/release-from-escrow)at your discretion. By default, funds are not held in escrow.

1. Java

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest()
  .amount(new BigDecimal("100.00"))
  .merchantAccountId("blue_ladders_store")
  .paymentMethodNonce(nonceFromTheClient)
  .options()
    .submitForSettlement()
    .holdInEscrow()
    .done()
  .serviceFeeAmount(new BigDecimal("10.00"))
  .done();
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.transaction().sale(request);
```

# Transaction: Sale
Source: https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/

## Transaction: Sale

[Transaction](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/response/transaction)response object. To create a transaction, you must include an

[amount](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/response/transaction/dotnet/#amount)and either a

[payment_method_nonce](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/response/transaction/dotnet/#payment_method_nonce), a

[PaymentMethodToken](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/response/transaction/dotnet/#payment_method_nonce), or a

[CustomerId](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/response/customer/dotnet#id). Passing a CustomerId is equivalent to passing the PaymentMethodToken of the customer's default payment method. Braintree offers products that manage risk and fraud related to each transaction. These products can only be leveraged if there is adequate data to support the capabilities. The required data can be easily added during the Braintree SDK or

[Graph QL](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/graphql/integration_guides/). integration, and must be done prior using risk products. For additional guidance go to

[Premium Fraud Management Tools](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/premium/overview). The following example creates a transaction using a

[PaymentMethodNonce](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#payment_method_nonce)from a client and instructs that it should be submitted for settlement immediately using

[Options.SubmitForSettlement](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#options-submit_for_settlement). You can see more

[examples](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#examples), including

[using a vaulted payment method](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#using-a-vaulted-payment-method), below the parameter reference.

1. DOTNET

```
var request = new TransactionRequest
{
    Amount = 10.00M,
    PaymentMethodNonce = nonceFromTheClient,
    DeviceData = deviceDataFromTheClient,
    Options = new TransactionOptionsRequest
    {
        SubmitForSettlement = true
    }
};
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.Transaction.Sale(request);
if (result.IsSuccess()) {
  // See result.Target for details
} else {
  // Handle errors
}
```

Results of a merchant-performed 3D Secure authentication. **You will only need to use these fields if you've performed your own integration with a 3D Secure MPI provider (e.g. Cardinal Centinel).** Otherwise, Braintree's SDKs handle this for you in [our standard 3D Secure integration](https://developer.paypal.com/guides/3d-secure/overview). You can use 3DS passthrough integration to enable the Visa Digital Commerce Authentication Program [(DCAP)](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/enhanced-data/enable-dcap) in the US, if you share DCAP data through your 3DS Data-Only solution.

Cardholder authentication verification value or CAVV. The main encrypted message issuers and card networks use to verify authentication has occurred. Mastercard uses an AVV message and American Express uses an AEVV message, each of which should also be passed in the Cavv parameter.

[DirectoryResponse](https://developer.paypal.com#three_d_secure_pass_thru-directory_response)[DsTransactionId](https://developer.paypal.com#three_d_secure_pass_thru-ds_transaction_id)
Transaction identifier resulting from 3D Secure 2 authentication. This field must be supplied for Mastercard Identity Check.

The value of the electronic commerce indicator (ECI) flag, which indicates the outcome of the 3DS authentication.

Accepted values for Mastercard:

- `00` = Failed or not attempted
- `01` = Attempted
- `02` = Success
- `04` = Data-Only (Applies to limited processors)

Accepted values for all other card brands:

- `07` = Failed or not attempted
- `06` = Attempted
- `05` = Success

Accepted values for Visa DCAP in the US:

- `07` = Data-Only

Specifies which payment network was used during 3D Secure authentication to ensure the transaction is routed to the same network for processing. Primarily used for dual-network cards (e.g., eftpos cards).

Accepted values (case-insensitive):

- `eftpos`
- `Visa`
- `Mastercard`

The version of 3D Secure authentication used for the transaction. Required
on Visa and Mastercard authentications. Must be composed of digits separated
by periods (e.g. `1.0.2`).

Transaction identifier resulting from 3D Secure authentication. Uniquely identifies the transaction and sometimes required in the authorization message. Must be base64-encoded. This field will no longer be used in 3D Secure 2 authentications.

Specifies the source of the transaction. The value passed depends on whether the transaction is initiated by the merchant or the customer. If the transaction is an ecommerce transaction initiated by the customer, no value is passed.

Accepted values for merchant-initiated transactions:

- `recurring` = Transactions for subsequent recurring payments (e.g. subscriptions with a fixed amount on a predefined schedule).
- `unscheduled` = Transactions for unscheduled payments that are not recurring on a predefined schedule or amount (e.g. balance top-up). Formerly`merchant` .
- `installment` = Transactions for subsequent installment payments. (e.g. when the customer makes a single large purchase and wants to make payments over time).

Accepted values for customer-initiated transactions:

- `recurring_first` = Transactions that represent the first in a series of recurring payments or subscription.
- `moto` = Transactions that are initiated by the customer via the merchant by mail or telephone.
- `installment_first` = Transactions that represent the first in a series of installment payments.
- `estimated` = Transactions that support subsequent incremental authorization.
- 'estimated_moto' = Transactions that are initiated by the customer via the merchant by mail or telephone that support subsequent incremental authorization.

Note: `installment` and `installment_first` may only be available in certain regions.  If installment transactions are not supported in your region, the transaction will automatically be categorized as `recurring`.

[ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)format.

## Examples

The following examples demonstrate common ways to create a transaction. Start with the full example, then review the additional examples for specific use cases.

### Full example

    Here is an example of passing in everything a typical merchant might use. Some parameters are
    mutually exclusive, so we'll show those in separate examples. If there is anything you want to store
    with the transaction details that we don't have a field for, you can always use

[Collect device data](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/premium-fraud-management-tools/client-side)from the client and include the DeviceDataFromTheClient in the transaction.

1. C#

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest
{
    Amount = 10.00M,
    OrderId = "order id",
    MerchantAccountId = "a_merchant_account_id",
    PaymentMethodNonce = nonceFromTheClient,
    DeviceData = deviceDataFromTheClient,
    Customer = new CustomerRequest
    {
        FirstName = "Drew",
        LastName = "Smith",
        Company = "Braintree",
        Phone = "312-555-1234",
        Fax = "312-555-1235",
        Website = "http://www.example.com",
        Email = "drew@example.com"
    },
    BillingAddress = new AddressRequest
    {
        FirstName = "Paul",
        LastName = "Smith",
        Company = "Braintree",
        StreetAddress = "1 E Main St",
        ExtendedAddress = "Suite 403",
        Locality = "Chicago",
        Region = "IL",
        PostalCode = "60622",
        CountryCodeAlpha2 = "US"
    },
    ShippingAddress = new AddressRequest
    {
        FirstName = "Jen",
        LastName = "Smith",
        Company = "Braintree",
        StreetAddress = "1 E 1st St",
        ExtendedAddress = "Suite 403",
        Locality = "Bartlett",
        Region = "IL",
        PostalCode = "60103",
        CountryCodeAlpha2 = "US"
    },
    Options = new TransactionOptionsRequest
    {
        SubmitForSettlement = true
    },
};
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.Transaction.Sale(request);
```
1. C#

```
if (result.IsSuccess())
{
    Transaction transaction = result.Target;
    Console.WriteLine(transaction.Type);   // TransactionType.CREDIT
    Console.WriteLine(transaction.Status); // TransactionStatus.SUBMITTED_FOR_SETTLEMENT
}
```
### Storing in your vault

    When creating a transaction, you can also store the payment method in your vault.
    #### Existing customer with new payment method

    To associate this transaction's payment method with an existing customer, pass a
    [CustomerId](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#customer_id)along with

[Options.StoreInVault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#options-store_in_vault)or

[Options.StoreInVaultOnSuccess](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#options-store_in_vault_on_success)as True.

1. C#

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest
{
    Amount = 10.00M,
    PaymentMethodNonce = nonceFromTheClient,
    CustomerId = "the_customer_id",
    Options = new TransactionOptionsRequest
    {
        StoreInVaultOnSuccess = true
    }
};
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.Transaction.Sale(request);
```
#### New customer with new payment method

    To store a payment method for a new customer, set
    [Options.StoreInVault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#options-store_in_vault)or

[Options.StoreInVaultOnSuccess](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#options-store_in_vault_on_success)to True on your transaction. You can optionally specify

[Customer](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#customer)parameters for your new customer, as well:

1. C#

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest
{
    Amount = 10.00M,
    PaymentMethodNonce = nonceFromTheClient,
    Customer = new CustomerRequest
    {
        Id = "a_customer_id"
    },
    Options = new TransactionOptionsRequest
    {
        StoreInVaultOnSuccess = true
    }
};
Result<Transaction> result = gateway.Transaction.Sale(request);
```
[Customer](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#customer)parameter should only be used when creating a new customer with a new payment method, and StoreInVaultOnSuccess only vaults the payment method if the transaction is successful.

### Using a vaulted payment method

    You can create a transaction using a payment method stored in the
    [Vault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/vault/overview)by passing a

1. C#

```
var result = gateway.Transaction.Sale(
    new TransactionRequest
    {
        PaymentMethodToken = "the_token",
        Amount = 10.00M
    });
```
[CustomerId](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#customer_id), which will use the customer's default payment method:

1. C#

```
var result = gateway.Transaction.Sale(
    new TransactionRequest
    {
        CustomerId = "the_customer_id",
        Amount = 10.00M
    });
```
### Using a CVV-only nonce

    To transact with a CVV-only nonce, use both a nonce representing the CVV **and**a

[PaymentMethodToken](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#payment_method_token)representing the vaulted payment method. To collect a CVV-only nonce, use the client SDKs to tokenize only the CVV property. See an example in our

1. C#

```
var result = gateway.Transaction.Sale(
    new TransactionRequest
    {
        PaymentMethodToken = "the_token",
        PaymentMethodNonce = cvvOnlyNonceFromClient,
        Amount = 10.00M
    });
```
### Specify merchant account ID

    To specify which merchant account to use, pass the
    [MerchantAccountId](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#merchant_account_id)when creating the transaction.

1. C#

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest
{
    Amount = 100.00M,
    MerchantAccountId = "your_merchant_account",
    PaymentMethodNonce = nonceFromTheClient
};

```
[Contact us](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/help?issue=TransactionProcessingQuestion)if you would like to change which merchant account is default.

### Using stored addresses

    You can use
    [addresses stored on a customer](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/address/create)by passing the address's ID. This works for both the shipping address and billing address.

1. C#

```
var result = gateway.Transaction.Sale(
    new TransactionRequest
    {
        CustomerId = "the_customer_id",
        Amount = 10.00M,
        BillingAddressId = "AA",
        ShippingAddressId = "AB"
    });
```
### Custom fields

    Whatever you
    [configure as the API name for your custom fields](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/custom-fields#creating-a-custom-field)will be used when setting them on the transaction. Here is an example of setting custom fields with API names of

`custom_field_one` and `custom_field_two`.
    1. C#

```
var result = gateway.Transaction.Sale(
    new TransactionRequest
    {
        Amount = 10.00M,
        PaymentMethodNonce = nonceFromTheClient,
        CustomFields = new Dictionary<string, string>
        {
            { "custom_field_one", "value one" },
            { "custom_field_two", "value two" }
        }
    });
if (result.IsSuccess())
{
  Dictionary<string, string> customFields = result.Target.CustomFields;
}
```
### Dynamic descriptors

    Dynamic descriptors are typically composed of a name and phone number or URL. The name must include
    the business name, followed by a product name or identifier, separated by an asterisk (*). Depending
    on the type of transaction you're creating, the length/character limits may differ from those previously outlined. For example, you can only specify up to 18 characters for dynamic descriptor names
    on Braintree Marketplace transactions. See below for details on [Venmo](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#venmo),

[PayPal](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#paypal), and

[Braintree Marketplace](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/dotnet/#braintree-marketplace)dynamic descriptors. Your processor may also restrict which descriptor values you can pass; certain processors allow you to pass URLs instead of phone numbers, while others accept only phone numbers or only names. If your processor supports URLs and you send both a phone number and URL, we will only pass the URL to the processor.

[Contact us](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/help?issue=updateDescriptor)for more information on your processor's specific requirements.

1. C#

```
Result<transaction> result = gateway.Transaction.Sale(
    new TransactionRequest {
        Amount = 10.00M,
        PaymentMethodNonce = nonceFromTheClient,
        Descriptor = new DescriptorRequest {
            Name = "company*my product",
            Phone = "3125551212",
            Url = "company.com"
        }
    }
);
Transaction transaction = result.Target;
<a href="http://transaction.Descriptor.Name">transaction.Descriptor.Name</a>;
// "company*my product"
transaction.Descriptor.Phone; // "3125551212"
```
#### Venmo

    Venmo only supports the dynamic descriptor `name`. The value can contain letters, numbers, spaces, and the characters  `+`, `-`, and `.`. Any other character causes the entire dynamic descriptor name to be ignored — for example, `O#1234` would result in the full descriptor being sent without a dynamic descriptor name.
    The full descriptor sent to the processor is made up of three parts:
    - 
            The fixed prefix `VENMO *` including two trailing spaces
- 
            The `Business Name` registered in your Venmo application form
- 
            The Dynamic Descriptor Name you submit through the `descriptor.name` field in your`transaction.sale()` or`transaction.submit_for_settlement()` call

`AStore` and you submit `O-1234` as the Dynamic Descriptor Name, the full descriptor is `VENMO *AStore O-1234`.
    When calling the API, submit only the dynamic portion (for example, O-1234) in the `descriptor.name` field. Do not include your Business Name or the VENMO * prefix — Venmo adds both automatically, and including them yourself will result in a duplicated or incorrect descriptor.
    `Business Name` and `Dynamic Descriptor Name` portion will be truncated as
        needed. If you want to change the `Business Name` of the descriptor, you can edit your
        Venmo profile through the Venmo Processing page in the Control Panel. This will also update the name
        displayed to customers in the Venmo app during transaction processing.
    #### PayPal

    For PayPal transactions only, the dynamic descriptor is limited to a total of 22 characters and includes the following
    elements:
- The default prefix of ```
                PAYPAL *
```
- Your PayPal hard descriptor*
- The product portion of your `name`

These rules apply only when the payment method is PayPal. Card and other payment methods follow their own descriptor rules.

**Depending on your PayPal account setup, the PayPal hard descriptor may not be included in the dynamic descriptor. You can update the hard descriptor value from your*

[PayPal console](https://www.paypal.com/login). They Name must meet the following guidelines:

- Must include your registered Doing Business As (DBA) name, followed by an asterisk and a product description
- The DBA portion must be 3, 7, or 12 characters long - this portion will be dropped from your dynamic descriptor

#### Braintree Marketplace
![AnchorIcon](https://www.paypalobjects.com/btdevdoc/bundles/4.41.0/_assets/anchor-PKYVW2VT.svg)

    The only dynamic descriptor value we will pass for Braintree Marketplace transactions is the
    Name you specify. We will not send any dynamic
    Phone or Url values to the processor, but we
    will pass the Phone from the hard descriptor on your master merchant
    account. The dynamic descriptor name can only contain the ASCII characters a-z, A-Z, the numbers
    0-9, and the characters `.-+` and spaces (it can't contain special characters like
    `Ñ`, `ü`, and `é`). The maximum length is 18 characters; we will
    truncate any longer strings. The descriptor we pass to the processor will start with
    `"BT *"`, followed by the Name you specify.
    - 
            If the specified name is 12 characters or fewer, the descriptor we pass to the processor will
            end with a randomly generated 6-character string, such as `123abc` , which identifies the
            sub-merchant:`BT *MYDESCRIPTOR123abc`
- 
            If the specified name is 13 characters or greater, the descriptor we pass to the processor will
            not end with a randomly generated 6-character string:
            `BT *MYDESCRIPTORISLONG`

### Hold a Braintree Marketplace transaction in escrow on creation
![AnchorIcon](https://www.paypalobjects.com/btdevdoc/bundles/4.41.0/_assets/anchor-PKYVW2VT.svg)

    Upon creating a
    [Braintree Marketplace transaction](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/braintree-marketplace/create), you can specify that its funds should be held in escrow. These funds can then be

[released](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/release-from-escrow)at your discretion. By default, funds are not held in escrow.

1. C#

```
TransactionRequest request = new TransactionRequest {
    Amount = 100.0m,
    MerchantAccountId = "blue_ladders_store",
    PaymentMethodNonce = nonceFromTheClient,
    Options = new TransactionOptionsRequest {
        SubmitForSettlement = true,
        HoldInEscrow = true
    },
    ServiceFeeAmount = 10.00m
};
Result<transaction> result = gateway.Transaction.Sale(request);
```

# Transaction: Sale
Source: https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/

## Transaction: Sale

[Transaction](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/response/transaction)response object. To create a transaction, you must include an

[amount](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#amount)and either a

[paymentMethodNonce](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#payment_method_nonce), a

[paymentMethodToken](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#payment_method_token), or a

[customerId](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#customer_id). Passing a customerId is equivalent to passing the paymentMethodToken of the customer's default payment method. Braintree offers products that manage risk and fraud related to each transaction. These products can only be leveraged if there is adequate data to support the capabilities. The required data can be easily added during the Braintree SDK or

[Graph QL](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/graphql/)integration, and must be done prior using risk products. For additional guidance go to

[Premium Fraud Management Tools](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/premium/overview). The following example creates a transaction using a

[paymentMethodNonce](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#payment_method_nonce)from a client and instructs that it should be submitted for settlement immediately using

[options.submitForSettlement](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#options-submit_for_settlement). You can see more

[examples](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#examples), including

[using a vaulted payment method](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#using-a-vaulted-payment-method), below the parameter reference.

1. PHP

```
$result = $gateway->transaction()->sale([
    'amount' => '10.00',
    'paymentMethodNonce' => $nonceFromTheClient,
    'deviceData' => $deviceDataFromTheClient,
    'options' => [
        'submitForSettlement' => True
    ]
]);
if ($result->success) {
    // See $result->transaction for details
} else {
    // Handle errors
}
```
##### Parameters

The billing amount of the request. This value must be greater than 0, and must match the currency format of the merchant account. Can only contain numbers and one decimal point (e.g. `x.xx`). Can't be greater than the maximum allowed by the processor. [Contact us](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/help?issue=TransactionProcessingQuestion) for your specific limit.

Specifies the source of the transaction. The value passed depends on whether the transaction is initiated by the merchant or the customer. If the transaction is an ecommerce transaction initiated by the customer, no value is passed.

Accepted values for merchant-initiated transactions:

- `recurring` = Transactions for subsequent recurring payments (e.g. subscriptions with a fixed amount on a predefined schedule).
- `unscheduled` = Transactions for unscheduled payments that are not recurring on a predefined schedule or amount (e.g. balance top-up). Formerly`merchant` .
- `installment` = Transactions for subsequent installment payments. (e.g. when the customer makes a single large purchase and wants to make payments over time).

Accepted values for customer-initiated transactions:

- `recurring_first` = Transactions that represent the first in a series of recurring payments or subscription.
- `moto` = Transactions that are initiated by the customer via the merchant by mail or telephone.
- `installment_first` = Transactions that represent the first in a series of installment payments.
- `estimated` = Transactions that support subsequent incremental authorization.
- 'estimated_moto' = Transactions that are initiated by the customer via the merchant by mail or telephone that support subsequent incremental authorization.

Note: `installment` and `installment_first` may only be available in certain regions.  If installment transactions are not supported in your region, the transaction will automatically be categorized as `recurring`.

[ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601)format.

## Examples

### Full example

    Here is an example of passing in everything a typical merchant might use. Some parameters are
    mutually exclusive, so we'll show those in separate examples. If there is anything you want to store
    with the transaction details that we don't have a field for, you can always use

[Collect device data](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/premium-fraud-management-tools/client-side)from the client and include the deviceDataFromTheClient in the transaction.

1. PHP

```
$result = $gateway->transaction()->sale([
    'amount' => '100.00',
    'orderId' => 'order id',
    'merchantAccountId' => 'a_merchant_account_id',
    'paymentMethodNonce' => $nonceFromTheClient,
    'deviceData' => $deviceDataFromTheClient,
    'customer' => [
        'firstName' => 'Drew',
        'lastName' => 'Smith',
        'company' => 'Braintree',
        'phone' => '312-555-1234',
        'fax' => '312-555-1235',
        'website' => 'http://www.example.com',
        'email' => 'drew@example.com'
    ],
    'billing' => [
        'firstName' => 'Paul',
        'lastName' => 'Smith',
        'company' => 'Braintree',
        'streetAddress' => '1 E Main St',
        'extendedAddress' => 'Suite 403',
        'locality' => 'Chicago',
        'region' => 'IL',
        'postalCode' => '60622',
        'countryCodeAlpha2' => 'US'
    ],
    'shipping' => [
        'firstName' => 'Jen',
        'lastName' => 'Smith',
        'company' => 'Braintree',
        'streetAddress' => '1 E 1st St',
        'extendedAddress' => 'Suite 403',
        'locality' => 'Bartlett',
        'region' => 'IL',
        'postalCode' => '60103',
        'countryCodeAlpha2' => 'US'
    ],
    'options' => [
        'submitForSettlement' => true
    ]
]);
```
1. PHP

```
$result->success; // true
$result->transaction->status; // e.g. 'submitted_for_settlement'
$result->transaction->type; // e.g. 'credit'
```
### Storing in Vault

    When creating a transaction, you can also store the payment method in your Vault.
    #### Existing customer with new payment method

    To associate this transaction's payment method with an existing customer, pass a
    [customerId](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#customer_id)along with

[options.storeInVault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#options-store_in_vault)or

[options.storeInVaultOnSuccess](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#options-store_in_vault_on_success)as true.

1. PHP

```
$result = $gateway->transaction()->sale([
    'amount' => '10.00',
    'paymentMethodNonce' => nonceFromTheClient,
    'customerId' => 'the_customer_id',
    'options' => [
        'storeInVaultOnSuccess' => true,
    ]
]);
```
#### New customer with new payment method

    To store a payment method for a new customer, set
    [options.storeInVault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#options-store_in_vault)or

[options.storeInVaultOnSuccess](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#options-store_in_vault_on_success)to true on your transaction. You can optionally specify

[customer](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#customer)parameters for your new customer, as well:

1. PHP

```
$result = $gateway->transaction()->sale([
    'amount' => '10.00',
    'paymentMethodNonce' => nonceFromTheClient,
    'customer' => [
        'id' => 'a_customer_id'
    ],
    'options' => [
        'storeInVaultOnSuccess' => true,
    ]
]);
```
[customer](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#customer)parameter should only be used when creating a new customer with a new payment method, and storeInVaultOnSuccess only vaults the payment method if the transaction is successful.

### Using a vaulted payment method

    You can create a transaction using a payment method stored in the
    [Vault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/vault/overview)by passing a

1. PHP

```
$result = $gateway->transaction()->sale([
    'paymentMethodToken' => 'the_payment_method_token',
    'amount' => '100.00'
]);
```
[customerId](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#customer_id), which will use the customer's default payment method:

1. PHP

```
$result = $gateway->transaction()->sale([
    'customerId' => 'the_customer_id',
    'amount' => '100.00'
]);
```
### Using a CVV-only nonce

    To transact with a CVV-only nonce, use both a nonce representing the CVV **and**a

[paymentMethodToken](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#payment_method_token)representing the vaulted payment method. To collect a CVV-only nonce, use the client SDKs to tokenize only the CVV property. See an example in our

1. PHP

```
$result = $gateway->transaction()->sale([
    'paymentMethodToken' => 'the_payment_method_token',
    'paymentMethodNonce' => cvvOnlyNonceFromClient,
    'amount' => '100.00'
]);
```
### Specify merchant account ID

    To specify which merchant account to use, pass the
    [merchantAccountId](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#merchant_account_id)when creating the transaction.

1. PHP

```
$result = $gateway->transaction()->sale([
    'amount' => '100.00',
    'merchantAccountId' => 'gbp_merchant_account',
    'paymentMethodNonce' => nonceFromTheClient
]);
```
[Contact us](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/help?issue=TransactionProcessingQuestion)if you would like to change which merchant account is default.

### Using stored addresses

    You can use
    [addresses stored on a customer](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/address/create)by passing the address's ID. This works for both the shipping address and billing address.

1. PHP

```
$result = $gateway->transaction()->sale([
    'customerId' => 'the_customer_id',
    'amount' => '100.00',
    'billingAddressId' => 'AA',
    'shippingAddressId' => 'AB'
]);
```
### Custom fields

    Whatever you
    [configure as the API name for your custom fields](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/custom-fields#creating-a-custom-field)will be used when setting them on the transaction. Here is an example of setting custom fields with API names of

`custom_field_one` and `custom_field_two`.
    1. PHP

```
$result = $gateway->transaction()->sale([
    'amount' => '100.00',
    'paymentMethodNonce' => nonceFromTheClient,
    'customFields' => [
        'custom_field_one' => 'custom value',
        'custom_field_two' => 'another custom value'
    ]
]);
$result->transaction->customFields['custom_field_one']
# 'custom value'
$result->transaction->customFields['custom_field_two']
# 'another custom value'
```
### Dynamic descriptors

    Dynamic descriptors are typically composed of a name and phone number or URL. The name must include
    the business name, followed by a product name or identifier, separated by an asterisk (*). Depending
    on the type of transaction you're creating, the length/character limits may differ from those
    outlined above. For example, you can only specify up to 18 characters for dynamic descriptor names
    on Braintree Marketplace transactions. See below for details on [Venmo](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#venmo),

[PayPal](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#paypal), and

[Braintree Marketplace](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#braintree-marketplace)dynamic descriptors. Your processor may also restrict which descriptor values you can pass; certain processors allow you to pass URLs instead of phone numbers, while others accept only phone numbers or only names. If your processor supports URLs and you send both a phone number and URL, we will only pass the URL to the processor.

[Contact us](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/help?issue=updateDescriptor)for more information on your processor's specific requirements.

1. PHP

```
$result = $gateway->transaction()->sale([
    'amount' => '10.00',
    'paymentMethodNonce' => nonceFromTheClient,
    'descriptor' => [
        'name' => 'company*my product',
        'phone' => '3125551212',
        'url' => 'company.com'
    ]
]);
$result->transaction->descriptor->name
# 'company*my product'
$result->transaction->descriptor->phone
# '3125551212'
```
#### Venmo

    Venmo only supports the dynamic descriptor `name`. Its format allows alpha-numeric
    characters and `+-.`  (space included); any other characters will result in the dynamic
    descriptor name not being included in the full descriptor sent to the processor. The full descriptor
    submitted to the processor is structured as follows:
- The default prefix of VENMO * (Two whitespaces).
- 
            The `Business Name` submitted in the[Venmo application form](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/payment-methods/venmo#go-live) .
- 
            The `Dynamic Descriptor Name` submitted in the[transaction.sale()](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/php/#descriptor-name) or[transaction.submit_for_settlement()](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/submit-for-settlement/php#descriptor) call.

`AStore` is the `Business Name` and `O-1234` is the
    `Dynamic Descriptor Name`. If the dynamic descriptor name contains invalid characters,
    e.g. 0#1234, the entire dynamic descriptor name will be ignored.
    `Business Name` and `Dynamic Descriptor Name` portion will be truncated as
        needed. If you want to change the `Business Name` of the descriptor, you can edit your
        Venmo profile via the Venmo Processing page in the Control Panel. This will also update the name
        displayed to customers in the Venmo app during transaction processing.
    #### PayPal

    For PayPal transactions only, the dynamic descriptor is limited to a total of 22 characters and includes the following
    elements:
- The default prefix of `PAYPAL *`
- Your PayPal hard descriptor*
- The product portion of your `name`

These rules apply only when the payment method is PayPal. Card and other payment methods follow their own descriptor rules.

**Depending on your PayPal account setup, the PayPal hard descriptor may not be included in the dynamic descriptor. You can update the hard descriptor value from your*

[PayPal console](https://www.paypal.com/login). The name must meet the following guidelines:

- Must include your registered Doing Business As (DBA) name, followed by an asterisk and a product description
- The DBA portion must be 3, 7 or 12 characters long - this portion will be dropped from your dynamic descriptor

#### Braintree Marketplace

    The only dynamic descriptor value we will pass for Braintree Marketplace transactions is the
    name you specify. We will not send any dynamic
    phone or url values to the processor, but we
    will pass the phone from the hard descriptor on your master merchant
    account. The dynamic descriptor name can only contain the ASCII characters a-z, A-Z, the numbers
    0-9, and the characters `.-+` and spaces (it can't contain special characters like
    `Ñ`, `ü`, and `é`). The maximum length is 18 characters; we will
    truncate any longer strings. The descriptor we pass to the processor will start with
    `"BT *"`, followed by the name you specify.
- 
            If the specified name is 12 characters or fewer, the descriptor we pass to the processor will
            end with a randomly generated 6-character string (e.g. `123abc` ) which identifies the
            sub-merchant:`BT *MYDESCRIPTOR123abc`
- 
            If the specified name is 13 characters or greater, the descriptor we pass to the processor will
            not end with a randomly generated 6-character string:
            `BT *MYDESCRIPTORISLONG`

### Hold a Braintree Marketplace transaction in escrow on creation

    Upon creating a
    [Braintree Marketplace transaction](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/braintree-marketplace/create), you can specify that its funds should be held in escrow. These funds can then be

[released](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/release-from-escrow)at your discretion. By default, funds are not held in escrow.

1. PHP

```
$result = $gateway->transaction()->sale([
    'amount' => '100.00',
    'merchantAccountId' => 'blue_ladders_store',
    'paymentMethodNonce' => nonceFromTheClient,
    'options' => [
        'submitForSettlement' => true,
        'holdInEscrow' => true,
    ],
    'serviceFeeAmount' => "10.00"
]);
```

# Transaction: Sale
Source: https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/

## Transaction: Sale

[Transaction](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/response/transaction)response object. To create a transaction, you must include an

[amount](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#amount)and either a

[payment_method_nonce](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#payment_method_nonce), a

[payment_method_token](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#payment_method_token), or a

[customer_id](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#customer_id). Passing a customer_id is equivalent to passing the payment_method_token of the customer's default payment method. Braintree offers products that manage risk and fraud related to each transaction. These products can only be leveraged if there is adequate data to support the capabilities. The required data can be easily added during the Braintree SDK or

[Graph QL](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/graphql/). integration, and must be done prior using risk products. For additional guidance go to

[Premium Fraud Management Tools](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/guides/fraud-tools/premium/overview). The following example creates a transaction using a

[payment_method_nonce](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#payment_method_nonce)from a client and instructs that it should be submitted for settlement immediately using

[options.submit_for_settlement](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#options-submit_for_settlement). You can see more

[examples](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#examples), including

[using a vaulted payment method](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#using-a-vaulted-payment-method), below the parameter reference.

1. Python

```
result = gateway.transaction.sale({
    "amount": "10.00",
    "payment_method_nonce": nonce_from_the_client,
    "device_data": device_data_from_the_client,
    "options": {
        "submit_for_settlement": True
    }
})
if result.is_success:
    # See result.transaction for details
else:
    # Handle errors
```

Specifies the source of the transaction. The value passed depends on whether the transaction is initiated by the merchant or the customer. If the transaction is an ecommerce transaction initiated by the customer, no value is passed.

Accepted values for merchant-initiated transactions:

- `recurring` = Transactions for subsequent recurring payments (e.g. subscriptions with a fixed amount on a predefined schedule).
- `unscheduled` = Transactions for unscheduled payments that are not recurring on a predefined schedule or amount (e.g. balance top-up). Formerly`merchant` .
- `installment` = Transactions for subsequent installment payments. (e.g. when the customer makes a single large purchase and wants to make payments over time).

Accepted values for customer-initiated transactions:

- `recurring_first` = Transactions that represent the first in a series of recurring payments or subscription.
- `moto` = Transactions that are initiated by the customer via the merchant by mail or telephone.
- `installment_first` = Transactions that represent the first in a series of installment payments.
- `estimated` = Transactions that support subsequent incremental authorization.
- 'estimated_moto' = Transactions that are initiated by the customer via the merchant by mail or telephone that support subsequent incremental authorization.

Note: `installment` and `installment_first` may only be available in certain regions.  If installment transactions are not supported in your region, the transaction will automatically be categorized as `recurring`.

## Examples

### Full example

    Here is an example of passing in everything a typical merchant might use. Some parameters are
    mutually exclusive, so we'll show those in separate examples. If there is anything you want to store
    with the transaction details that we don't have a field for, you can always use

[Collect device data](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/premium-fraud-management-tools/client-side)from the client and include the device_data_from_the_client in the transaction.

1. Python

```
result = gateway.transaction.sale({
    "amount": "10.00",
    "order_id": "order id",
    "merchant_account_id": "a_merchant_account_id",
    "payment_method_nonce": nonce_from_the_client,
    "device_data": device_data_from_the_client,
    "customer": {
        "first_name": "Drew",
        "last_name": "Smith",
        "company": "Braintree",
        "phone": "312-555-1234",
        "fax": "312-555-1235",
        "website": "http://www.example.com",
        "email": "drew@example.com"
    },
    "billing": {
        "first_name": "Paul",
        "last_name": "Smith",
        "company": "Braintree",
        "street_address": "1 E Main St",
        "extended_address": "Suite 403",
        "locality": "Chicago",
        "region": "IL",
        "postal_code": "60622",
        "country_code_alpha2": "US"
    },
    "shipping": {
        "first_name": "Jen",
        "last_name": "Smith",
        "company": "Braintree",
        "street_address": "1 E 1st St",
        "extended_address": "Suite 403",
        "locality": "Bartlett",
        "region": "IL",
        "postal_code": "60103",
        "country_code_alpha2": "US"
    },
    "options": {
        "submit_for_settlement": True
    }
})
```
1. Python

```
result.is_success  # True
result.transaction.type  # "credit"
result.transaction.status  # "submitted_for_settlement"
```
### Storing in Vault

    When creating a transaction, you can also store the payment method in your Vault.
    #### Existing customer with new payment method

    To associate this transaction's payment method with an existing customer, pass a
    [customer_id](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#customer_id)along with

[options.store_in_vault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#options-store_in_vault)or

[options.store_in_vault_on_success](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#options-store_in_vault_on_success)as true.

1. Python

```
result = gateway.transaction.sale({
    "amount": "10.00",
    "payment_method_nonce": nonce_from_the_client,
    "customer_id": "the_customer_id",
    "options": {
        "store_in_vault_on_success": True,
    }
})
```
#### New customer with new payment method

    To store a payment method for a new customer, set
    [options.store_in_vault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#options-store_in_vault)or

[options.store_in_vault_on_success](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#options-store_in_vault_on_success)to true on your transaction. You can optionally specify

[customer](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#customer)parameters for your new customer, as well:

1. Python

```
result = gateway.transaction.sale({
    "amount": "10.00",
    "payment_method_nonce": nonce_from_the_client,
    "customer": {
        "id": "a_customer_id"
    },
    "options": {
        "store_in_vault_on_success": True,
    }
})
```
[customer](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#customer)parameter should only be used when creating a new customer with a new payment method, and store_in_vault_on_success only vaults the payment method if the transaction is successful.

### Using a vaulted payment method

    You can create a transaction using a payment method stored in the
    [Vault](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/vault/overview)by passing a

1. Python

```
result = gateway.transaction.sale({
    "payment_method_token": "the_token",
    "amount": "10.00"
})
```
[customer_id](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#customer_id), which will use the customer's default payment method:

1. Python

```
result = gateway.transaction.sale({
    "customer_id": "the_customer_id",
    "amount": "10.00"
})
```
### Using a CVV-only nonce

    To transact with a CVV-only nonce, use both a nonce representing the CVV **and**a

[payment_method_token](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#payment_method_token)representing the vaulted payment method. To collect a CVV-only nonce, use the client SDKs to tokenize only the CVV property. See an example in our

1. Python

```
result = gateway.transaction.sale({
    "payment_method_token": "the_token",
    "payment_method_nonce": cvvOnlyNonceFromClient,
    "amount": "10.00"
})
```
### Specify merchant account ID

    To specify which merchant account to use, pass the
    [merchant_account_id](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#merchant_account_id)when creating the transaction.

1. Python

```
result = gateway.transaction.sale({
    "amount": "100.00",
    "merchant_account_id": "your_merchant_account",
    "payment_method_nonce": nonce_from_the_client
})
```
[Contact us](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/help?issue=TransactionProcessingQuestion)if you would like to change which merchant account is default.

### Using stored addresses

    You can use
    [addresses stored on a customer](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/address/create)by passing the address's ID. This works for both the shipping address and billing address.

1. Python

```
result = gateway.transaction.sale({
    "customer_id": "the_customer_id",
    "amount": "10.00",
    "billing_address_id": "AA",
    "shipping_address_id": "AB"
})
```
### Custom fields

    Whatever you
    [configure as the API name for your custom fields](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/articles/control-panel/custom-fields#creating-a-custom-field)will be used when setting them on the transaction. Here is an example of setting custom fields with API names of

`custom_field_one` and `custom_field_two`.
    1. Python

```
result = gateway.transaction.sale({
    "amount": "100.00",
    "payment_method_nonce": nonce_from_the_client,
    "custom_fields": {
        "custom_field_one": "value one",
        "custom_field_two": "value two"
    }
})
if result.is_success:
    result.transaction.custom_fields  # {"custom_field_one": "value one", "custom_field_two": "value two"}
```
### Dynamic descriptors

    Dynamic descriptors are typically composed of a name and phone number or URL. The name must include
    the business name, followed by a product name or identifier, separated by an asterisk (*). Depending
    on the type of transaction you're creating, the length/character limits may differ from those
    outlined above. For example, you can only specify up to 18 characters for dynamic descriptor names
    on Braintree Marketplace transactions. See below for details on [Venmo](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#venmo),

[PayPal](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#paypal), and

[Braintree Marketplace](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale/python/#braintree-marketplace)dynamic descriptors. Your processor may also restrict which descriptor values you can pass; certain processors allow you to pass URLs instead of phone numbers, while others accept only phone numbers or only names. If your processor supports URLs and you send both a phone number and URL, we will only pass the URL to the processor.

[Contact us](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/help?issue=updateDescriptor)for more information on your processor's specific requirements.

1. Python

```
result = gateway.transaction.sale({
    "amount": "10.00",
    "payment_method_nonce": nonce_from_the_client,
    "descriptor": {
        "name": "company*my product",
        "phone": "3125551212",
        "url": "company.com"
    }
})
result.transaction.descriptor.name
# "company*my product"
result.transaction.descriptor.phone
# "3125551212"
```
#### Venmo

   Venmo only supports the dynamic descriptor `name`. The value can contain letters, numbers, spaces, and the characters  `+`, `-`, and `.`. Any other character causes the entire dynamic descriptor name to be ignored — for example, `O#1234` would result in the full descriptor being sent without a dynamic descriptor name.
    The full descriptor sent to the processor is made up of three parts:
    - 
            The fixed prefix `VENMO *` (including two trailing spaces)
- 
            The `Business Name` registered in your Venmo application form
- 
            The Dynamic Descriptor Name you submit through the `descriptor.name` field in your`transaction.sale()` or`transaction.submit_for_settlement()` call

`AStore` and you submit `O-1234` as the Dynamic Descriptor Name, the full descriptor is `VENMO *AStore O-1234`.
    When calling the API, submit only the dynamic portion (for example, O-1234) in the `descriptor.name` field. Do not include your Business Name or the VENMO * prefix — Venmo adds both automatically, and including them yourself will result in a duplicated or incorrect descriptor.
    `Business Name` and `Dynamic Descriptor Name` portion will be truncated as
        needed. If you want to change the `Business Name` of the descriptor, you can edit your
        Venmo profile via the Venmo Processing page in the Control Panel. This will also update the name
        displayed to customers in the Venmo app during transaction processing.
    #### PayPal

    For PayPal transactions only, the dynamic descriptor is limited to a total of 22 characters and includes the following
    elements:
    - The default prefix of `PAYPAL *`
- Your PayPal hard descriptor*
- The product portion of your `name`

These rules apply only when the payment method is PayPal. Card and other payment methods follow their own descriptor rules.

**Depending on your PayPal account setup, the PayPal hard descriptor may not be included in the dynamic descriptor. You can update the hard descriptor value from your*

[PayPal console](https://www.paypal.com/login). The name must meet the following guidelines:

- Must include your registered Doing Business As (DBA) name, followed by an asterisk and a product description
- The DBA portion must be 3, 7 or 12 characters long - this portion will be dropped from your dynamic descriptor

#### Braintree Marketplace

    The only dynamic descriptor value we will pass for Braintree Marketplace transactions is the
    name you specify. We will not send any dynamic
    phone or url values to the processor, but we
    will pass the phone from the hard descriptor on your master merchant
    account. The dynamic descriptor name can only contain the ASCII characters a-z, A-Z, the numbers
    0-9, and the characters `.-+` and spaces (it can't contain special characters like
    `Ñ`, `ü`, and `é`). The maximum length is 18 characters; we will
    truncate any longer strings. The descriptor we pass to the processor will start with
    `"BT *"`, followed by the name you specify.
- 
            If the specified name is 12 characters or fewer, the descriptor we pass to the processor will
            end with a randomly generated 6-character string (e.g. `123abc` ) which identifies the
            sub-merchant:`BT *MYDESCRIPTOR123abc`
- 
            If the specified name is 13 characters or greater, the descriptor we pass to the processor will
            not end with a randomly generated 6-character string:
            `BT *MYDESCRIPTORISLONG`

### Hold a Braintree Marketplace transaction in escrow on creation

    Upon creating a
    [Braintree Marketplace transaction](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/braintree-marketplace/create), you can specify that its funds should be held in escrow. These funds can then be

[released](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/release-from-escrow)at your discretion. By default, funds are not held in escrow.

1. Python

```
result = gateway.transaction.sale({
    "amount": "100.00",
    "merchant_account_id": "blue_ladders_store",
    "payment_method_nonce": nonce_from_the_client,
    "options": {
        "submit_for_settlement": True,
        "hold_in_escrow": True,
    },
    "service_fee_amount": "10.00"
})
```

# Troubleshooting and FAQ
Source: https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/hosted-fields/faq/javascript/v3

# Troubleshooting and FAQ

#### Can I verify the CVV when a customer uses or updates a vaulted card?

Set up Hosted Fields as you normally would, but this time, only specify cvv in the [top-level options](https://braintree.github.io/braintree-web/3.92.1/module-braintree-web_hosted-fields.html#.create):

1. Callback
2. Promise

```
// ...
braintree.hostedFields.create({
  // ...
  fields: {
    cvv: { container: '#cvv' }
  }
}, /* ... */);
```
To transact with a CVV-only nonce, see the [`Transaction.Sale()` examples](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/request/transaction/sale#using-a-cvv-only-nonce).

#### Why are media queries not being applied inside the frames?

Media queries are injected as-is into the hosted fields. This means that any media queries will use the iframe viewport as their reference instead of the parent page.

#### Can I use a dropdown (<select>) for a field?

You can use dropdowns for expiration month and expiration year fields.

1. Callback
2. Promise

```
// ...
braintree.hostedFields.create({
  // ...
  fields: {
    // ...
    expirationMonth: {
      container: '#expiration-month',
      placeholder: 'Expiration month',
      select: {
        options: [
          '01 - January',
          '02 - February',
          '03 - March',
          '04 - April',
          '05 - May',
          '06 - June',
          '07 - July',
          '08 - August',
          '09 - September',
          '10 - October',
          '11 - November',
          '12 - December'
        ]
      }
    },
    expirationYear: {
      container: '#expiration-year',
      placeholder: 'Expiration year',
      select: true
    }
  }
}, /* ... */);
```
#### Why do I need to use<div>elements in my form?

Hosted Fields provides synthetic input elements inside of iframes on your page. Using a <div> as opposed to an <input> allows us to inject iframes with limited side-effects.

#### Why does my field not look like a normal<input>?

Any styles applied to a <div> on your page will also be applied to your Hosted Fields. You might want to try adding a height or border value to your CSS to make each <div> look more like an <input>. For additional styling ideas, check out our [Hosted Fields examples](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/guides/hosted-fields/examples).

#### On iOS, why does clicking a label not focus the field?

Clicking on a <label> will still focus the input as usual on all browsers, except for iOS where we disable its buggy behavior.

## Frequent errors

#### Selector does not reference a valid DOM node

Hosted Fields requires valid CSS2 selectors or DOM nodes for each field declaration.

1. Callback
2. Promise

```
// ...
braintree.hostedFields.create({
  // ...
  fields: {
    number: { container: '#number' },
    expirationDate: { container: '#expiration-date' }
  }
}, /* ... */);
```
#### Hosted Fields may exhibit unexpected behavior when testing in sites such as CodePen, JS Bin, JSFiddle and others

These sites are known to use [aggressive sandboxing for their iframes](http://blog.codepen.io/2014/02/17/can-iframes-annoying-free/) (not a bad thing), which can potentially restrict many functions of Hosted Fields.

We recommend testing your integration outside of these JS sandbox sites to see if the unwanted behavior persists.
